title: Data centers are turning to old jet engines as the wait for power grows

description: Stuck in years-long lines for grid connections and new turbines, some AI data centers are making their own electricity with converted jet engines, the New York Times reported Tu...
content:
Stuck in years-long lines for grid connections and new turbines, some AI data centers are making their own electricity with converted jet engines, the New York Times reported Tuesday.

The engines, pulled from retired aircraft and rebuilt to burn natural gas, aren’t anyone’s idea of a permanent power plant. But they’re another sign of how far power supply has fallen behind the AI buildout.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

For companies stuck in those lines, the main draw of converted jet engines is how quickly the engines can be up and running. “It’s all about getting power as fast as possible,” Rystad Energy analyst Audun Martinsen told the Times. With jet-powered units, “they can have a data center running in 24 months,” he said.

Hooking up 100 megawatts to the grid in Northern Virginia, by comparison, takes about seven years, according to the International Energy Agency. Most power capacity is expected to come on by 2031, an executive at Mitsubishi Power, one of the world’s top makers of power generation equipment told Bloomberg last week.

In some cases, these delays are already costing some data center operators business. Last month, Microsoft pulled out as the anchor customer for Nscale’s data center in Loughton, England, after the local utility said it couldn’t deliver enough power until the early-to-mid 2030s.

Elon Musk’s xAI is among the companies already using the engines, having installed eight converted jet-engine turbines in Mississippi to help power its Colossus 2 data center in Memphis, the Times reported, citing state permits and satellite imagery. The units come from ProEnergy, which rebuilds a GE engine commonly found on Boeing jets.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

In 2025, OpenAI followed Musk’s lead with gas turbines at its first Stargate site in Abilene, Texas. Crusoe, a Denver-based startup that builds AI data centers, is constructing that Abilene campus and ordered 13 of ProEnergy’s converted units in April.

In September, Crusoe walked away from a $1.25 billion deal to buy 29 natural gas turbines from Boom Supersonic, a startup developing a supersonic passenger jet that has also begun selling a version of that jet’s engine as a power plant for data centers. A Crusoe spokesperson told TechCrunch at the time that the company still plans to use turbines.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Currently the Trump administration is adding to the pressure by encouraging data centers to generate their own electricity.

Converted jet engines come with trade-offs, though: They’re less efficient and pollute more than turbines designed for conventional gas plants and it takes more of them to make the same amount of power, according to the Times. That may ultimately make converted jet engines a short-term play with some experts saying that efficiency and environmental concerns may grow in importance in a year or two.

title: Barca thrash Villa 3-0 to halt perfect Champions League start
excerpt: Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the competition.
description: Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the competition.
content:
Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the competition.

Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth.

Unai Emery’s Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca’s greater ability in the final third.

The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world.

Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to.

The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute.

The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes’s effort.

Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca’s pressing.

Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end.

Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner.

Cancelo powered a strike narrowly over before setting up Raphinha for Barcelona’s third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal of the season across all competitions.

Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games.

title: 2027: APC restricts ministers to campaign rallies in home states
excerpt: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has directed ministers, political appointees and members of its 2027 campaign council to attend only rallies organise...
description: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has directed ministers, political appointees and members of its 2027 campaign council to attend only rallies organise...
content:
The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has directed ministers, political appointees and members of its 2027 campaign council to attend only rallies organised in their respective home states.

The directive was contained in a circular dated Tuesday which was signed by the Director-General of the council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari Abubakar.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The circular, addressed to all directors and heads of directorates, outlined guidelines for participation in the party’s presidential campaign rallies across the states and geopolitical zones.

Explaining the rationale for the directive, the council said, “As the 2027 Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) intensifies its campaign activities across the states and geopolitical zones, it is imperative to provide clear guidelines on participation at campaign rallies for strict compliance.”

It described the rallies as platforms for mobilising support for the party and communicating the President’s achievements to voters.

“Campaign rallies are intended to energise the base of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the states and zones, and to communicate the achievements of His Excellency, the President, to the electorate,” the circular stated.

It added, “Participation should therefore be organised in a manner that advances these objectives.”

The council directed directorates without specific responsibilities at the rallies to concentrate on their assigned duties, stating that they “are hereby directed to remain focused on the implementation of their approved Work Plans and Budgets.”

Ministers and other political appointees were specifically instructed to limit their participation to rallies in their home states.

“They are required to attend only the rallies held in their home states,” the circular stated.

It further directed them to “focus on grassroots mobilisation across their polling units, wards and Local Government Areas (LGAs), in line with the pyramid concept of the campaign plan to ensure targeted coordination and implementation.”

The restriction also applies to members of the Presidential Campaign Council, who were directed to attend only rallies in their home states and concentrate on implementing their directorates’ approved work plans.

According to the circular, they are expected to “focus on the implementation of their Directorate’s approved Work Plans and grassroots mobilisation across polling units, wards, and LGAs.”

For members of the APC National Working Committee, the council directed them to concentrate on party responsibilities and mobilisation in their respective states and geopolitical zones.

The circular stated that members of the committee, “with the exception of the National Chairman, National Secretary, National Women’s Leader, National Youth Leader, and National Organising Secretary,” were expected to attend rallies held in their home states.

The council also disclosed plans to give greater prominence to the party’s legislative candidates during the rallies.

It stated, “The Council seeks to strengthen the visibility of the APC State Assembly, House of Representatives, and Senatorial candidates at the rallies.”

Directors were subsequently instructed to ensure that all officers under their respective directorates were informed of the guidelines.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Directors are requested to ensure that the contents of this circular are brought to the attention of all officers within their Directorates and that its provisions are duly observed,” the document added.

The directive comes about three weeks after President Bola Tinubu announced that he would not attend every APC campaign rally ahead of the 2027 general election, citing the demands of governance and the country’s financial obligations.

Speaking on October 14, 2026, during the inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, Tinubu asked members to lead the party’s mobilisation efforts across the country while he attended to state responsibilities.

“You’ve warned me not to allow the rigour of the campaign to distract me from governance, I hear you. I am in full agreement with your decision. Nigeria needs more attention now,” he said.

He also told the campaign council that he would be unable to accompany members to every campaign event.

“So, you will excuse me from going everywhere with you, we have bills to pay. The American creditors cannot wait,” the President said.

Tinubu, however, assured party members that he would still make time to address Nigerians directly while they coordinated campaigns across states and local government areas.

“However, I will still make time to speak directly with Nigerians, even as you lead the campaign in the states and local government areas,” he added.

The APC subsequently outlined a nationwide campaign timetable covering the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with Tinubu scheduled to lead rallies in 12 states, including Rivers, Plateau, Oyo, Borno, Enugu, Bauchi, Sokoto, Delta, Kano and Adamawa.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Lagos is scheduled to host the grand finale on January 9, 2027.

The latest circular concluded by thanking party officials for their cooperation and commitment to the campaign, saying, “Thank you for your cooperation and continued commitment to the success of the campaign.”

title: UCL: Cunha double helps Man Utd beat Roma as Bayern beat Atletico 2-0
excerpt: Manchester United staged a remarkable second-half comeback to defeat Roma 3–2 at Old Trafford, while Bayern Munich and Barcelona also recorded victories in Tuesday’s UEFA Champi...
description: Manchester United staged a remarkable second-half comeback to defeat Roma 3–2 at Old Trafford, while Bayern Munich and Barcelona also recorded victories in Tuesday’s UEFA Champi...
content:
Manchester United staged a remarkable second-half comeback to defeat Roma 3–2 at Old Trafford, while Bayern Munich and Barcelona also recorded victories in Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League fixtures.

United overturned a two-goal deficit to secure all three points after Matheus Cunha scored twice late in the encounter, ending the visitors’ hopes of a memorable away victory.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Roma took an early lead in the 11th minute through Matías Soulé before Donyell Malen doubled their advantage from the penalty spot seven minutes later.

The visitors went into the break with a comfortable 2–0 lead, leaving United with a difficult task in the second half.

However, Bruno Fernandes reduced the deficit in the 58th minute with a penalty after an initial attempt was saved and ordered to be retaken following encroachment.

Cunha then brought United level in the 83rd minute before completing the turnaround three minutes later to give the hosts a 3–2 lead.

The Brazilian’s night ended on a sour note, however, as he was sent off after receiving a second yellow card in stoppage time.

The victory provided relief for manager Michael Carrick, whose side had been under pressure following a difficult run of results.

In Madrid, Bayern Munich defeated Atletico Madrid 2–0 to strengthen their position in the competition.

Eighteen-year-old Lennart Karl opened the scoring in the 54th minute, finishing after winning possession inside the penalty area and lifting the ball over goalkeeper Jan Oblak.

Konrad Laimer sealed the victory in the 74th minute with a powerful finish, ensuring the German champions returned home with all three points.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The result maintained Bayern’s unbeaten run in the competition after their previous two draws.

Meanwhile, Barcelona defeated Aston Villa 3–0 at Camp Nou, with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha providing the goals.

Yamal opened the scoring in the seventh minute after capitalising on a defensive error, giving the hosts an early advantage.

Raphinha doubled Barcelona’s lead in the 52nd minute before completing his brace in the 64th minute following an assist from Joao Cancelo.

The victory ended Aston Villa’s 100 per cent record in the Champions League, while Barcelona continued their impressive scoring form in the competition.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Tuesday’s other results saw Inter Milan defeat Feyenoord 3–0, Galatasaray beat Stuttgart 2–0, Sporting CP overcome Shakhtar Donetsk 1–0 and LASK thrash Slovan Bratislava 4–0.

Bodo/Glimt and Lille played out a goalless draw, while Paris Saint-Germain recorded the biggest victory of the night with a 6–0 demolition of Villarreal.

title: DSS denies plotting Sokoto protest, orders probe
excerpt: The Department of State Services (DSS) has denied allegations that it planned to organise protests in Sokoto State, describing the claim by former Vice President and African Dem...
description: The Department of State Services (DSS) has denied allegations that it planned to organise protests in Sokoto State, describing the claim by former Vice President and African Dem...
content:
The Department of State Services (DSS) has denied allegations that it planned to organise protests in Sokoto State, describing the claim by former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as inconsistent with its operations.

The Service, however, said its Director-General had ordered an investigation into the allegation in deference to the former vice president.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Deputy Director, Public Relations and Strategic Communications, Favour Dozie, the DSS said its operatives deployed to protect the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Mannir Daniya, evacuated him to safety when he was attacked on October 31, 2026.

According to the Service, Daniya escaped unhurt during the incident, while two DSS operatives were assaulted and were still receiving treatment in hospital as of the time of the statement.

The DSS said the governorship candidate personally contacted the State Director of the Service in Sokoto to express appreciation for the intervention and subsequently requested additional security reinforcement.

The Service also cited its arrest and prosecution of Monday Udeme Steven in Rivers State on March 2, 2026, for allegedly threatening to attack the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi.

It said Steven was prosecuted before a Federal High Court in Rivers State and sentenced to two years’ imprisonment.

The DSS said its operations to protect politicians across party lines contradicted Atiku’s allegation, which it argued could demoralise its operatives risking their lives in the line of duty.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

It nevertheless said the Director-General had ordered an investigation into the allegation out of respect for the former vice president.

The Service also recalled a similar allegation by African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, that it was involved in an attack on him in Ekiti State.

It said it appreciated the police for their swift investigation and preliminary report on the incident, which identified an altercation as its cause and led to the arrest of 11 suspects.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The DSS added that it would await the outcome of the police investigation and would not dissipate further energy on the matter.

The Service reaffirmed its commitment to accountability under its current Director-General.

title: Inter End Champions League Slump With 3-0 Win Over Feyenoord
excerpt: Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike ...
description: Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike ...
content:
Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike from German defender Yann Bisseck.

The three-time champions of Europe had lost their first two group games, but had far too much quality for a disappointing Feyenoord, who had little answer to Inter’s pace and attacking ability.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

On a clear and crisp evening in Rotterdam, the visitors quickly silenced the ever raucous crowd in De Kuip, piling on sustained pressure that paid dividends as early as the eighth minute.

Bisseck was given too much space on the edge of the box, allowed to turn and drill a sumptuous curling left-footed shot low past the diving Tjark Ernst in the Feyenoord goal.

Feyenoord struggled to break out of the Inter Milan high press and the Serie A champions dominated possession and territory for much of the first quarter.

The home fans had to wait for half an hour before their side produced their first effort of note, a clever one-two playing in Anis Hadj Moussa, who saw his shot blocked.

And Inter doubled their advantage shortly afterwards.

England international Djed Spence found himself in acres of space on the right hand side. His shot looped up off a defender, allowing Pio Esposito to bundle in with his head from short range.

The beginning of the second half brought more misery for Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s men, as Feyenoord’s defence backed off and invited an advancing Piotr Zielinski to shoot.

The Polish international midfielder gratefully accepted the invitation, firing home an unstoppable drive off the post on 54 minutes.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

With the game effectively over as a contest, Inter boss Cristian Chivu rang the changes, bringing off star striker Marcus Thuram.

Halfway through the second half, fireworks launched from outside the stadium landed on the pitch and roof, causing a short interruption.

And the match itself rather fizzled out, as Inter cruised and Feyenoord failed to find any spark to penetrate the Italian defences.

The win saw Inter climb to a more respectable place in the middle of the Champions League table while Feyenoord’s solitary victory leaves them adrift of the knock-out phase.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Feyenoord’s next Champions League encounter is a home tie against Porto, while Inter Milan welcome Stuttgart.

description: The Department of State Services has ordered an investigation into an allegation by former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar,...
content:
The Department of State Services has ordered an investigation into an allegation by former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, that the agency is planning to organise protests in Sokoto State.

The secret police said the investigation was ordered by its Director-General, Oluwatosin Ajayi, despite describing the allegation as inconsistent with its operations to protect political actors across party lines.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Multiple reports had noted on Tuesday that Atiku while fielding questions from journalists in Abuja accused the leadership of the DSS, of recruiting protesters to create disorder in Sokoto and provide a pretext for imposing a curfew to stop the party’s campaign rally.

However, in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Deputy Director, Public Relations and Strategic Communications, Favour Dozie, the DSS said its “operatives rescued the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Mannir Daniya, during an attack on October 31, 2026.”

According to the Service, its operatives “deployed to protect Daniya evacuated him to safety during the incident, while two DSS personnel were assaulted and were still receiving treatment in hospital as of Tuesday.”

The agency added that “Daniya personally contacted the State Director of the DSS in Sokoto to express appreciation and requested additional security reinforcement.”

PUNCH Online had earlier reported that the All Progressives Congress and the ADC in Sokoto State on Saturday traded accusations over an alleged attack on the convoy of the ADC governorship candidate Dan’iya.

The DSS also cited its arrest and prosecution of a man, Monday Udeme Steven, in Rivers State on March 2, 2026, over an alleged threat to attack the presidential candidate of the New Democratic Congress, Peter Obi.

It said “Steven was prosecuted at a Federal High Court in Rivers State and sentenced to two years’ imprisonment.”

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The Service said the operations demonstrated its commitment to protecting political actors irrespective of their party affiliations, but acknowledged that Atiku’s allegation had prompted the DG to order an investigation.

“Though these operations to protect all Political Parties is at variance with the elder statesman’s allegation and tend to demoralize our gallant operatives who are risking their lives in the line of duty, the DGDSS has still ordered an investigation into the allegation in deference to the elder statesman,” the statement read.

The DSS also referred to a similar allegation by the African Action Congress presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, who accused the agency of involvement in an attack on him in Ekiti State.

It said it welcomed the police investigation into the incident, which, according to the DSS, produced a preliminary report identifying an “altercation” as the cause and led to the arrest of 11 suspects.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The Service said it was awaiting the outcome of the police investigation and would not expend further energy on the matter.

“The Service will continue to remain accountable under the present DG,” the statement added.

---

title: 55,000 inmates awaiting trial in Nigeria — PPDC
excerpt: The Public and Private Development Centre has said about 55,000 inmates are awaiting trial in Nigerian correctional centres, raising concerns over prolonged detention and limite...
description: The Public and Private Development Centre has said about 55,000 inmates are awaiting trial in Nigerian correctional centres, raising concerns over prolonged detention and limite...
content:
The Public and Private Development Centre has said about 55,000 inmates are awaiting trial in Nigerian correctional centres, raising concerns over prolonged detention and limited access to legal representation.

The organisation’s Chief Executive Officer, Lucy Abagi, disclosed this on Tuesday at its Third Annual Law for Humanity Summit 2026 in Abuja, where she said the high cost of legal services had left many indigent Nigerians unable to secure lawyers.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Abagi said the organisation had secured bail for more than 8,500 Nigerians and prevented about 20,000 others from being admitted into correctional facilities through its interventions over the past four years.

She said the 55,000 figure represented inmates in Nigerian Correctional Service facilities for which the organisation had data, adding that it did not cover every detention facility in the country.

“Of course you know that the cost of hiring a legal representation in Nigeria is quite high. And how many Nigerians can afford this? So PPDC is adopting different strategies, using low-cost effective measures to ensure that we have lawyers representing Nigerians across different detention centres.

“And I’d like to say that there are different detention centres in Nigeria, but as of this moment, we only have data that represents the Nigerian Correctional Centres, and of course that is about 55,000 awaiting trial inmates,” she said.

Figures published by the Nigerian Correctional Service showed that 53,670 inmates were awaiting trial as of June 29, 2026, out of a total custodial population of 82,195. The awaiting-trial population accounted for about 65 per cent of inmates in the facilities at the time.

Abagi said PPDC had supported about 11 university law clinics in the past four years, working with pro bono lawyers and police solicitors to review case files and assist detainees.

She expressed concern that some people had remained in custody for periods longer than the possible sentences for the offences they were accused of committing, without their cases being concluded.

The PPDC chief executive said the organisation was working to sustain the interventions despite funding challenges, and called on development partners, philanthropists and members of the public to support efforts to improve access to justice.

The summit, themed ‘Justice in the Age of Data and AI’, brought together representatives of the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria, the Nigerian Bar Association, pro bono lawyers and university law clinics to examine how technology could improve access to legal services.

Speaking at the event, a Professor of Law and President of the Centre for Socio-Legal Studies, Yemi Akinseye-George, warned that the use of artificial intelligence in the justice system must be regulated to prevent it from worsening inequality.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He said AI could help bridge the gap between wealthy and indigent Nigerians but should not replace the responsibilities of lawyers and judges.

“AI has come to stay and we must recognise it as a tool for advancing justice, as a tool for bridging the gap between the poor and the rich,” he said.

He cautioned legal practitioners against relying excessively on the technology, stressing that they remained responsible for the accuracy of their work.

“Humans must be in control. We must take responsibility and we must put in place effective mechanisms for regulating AI to make sure that it does not become another instrument for oppression, another instrument for widening the gap between the rich and the poor,” he added.

The Director-General of the Legal Aid Council, Aliyu Abubakar, represented by his Technical Assistant, Bamidele Ibikunle, also urged lawyers and judges to verify information generated by AI before relying on it in legal proceedings.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He warned that lawyers could end up citing non-existent or inaccurate court decisions if they failed to check AI-generated references against authoritative law reports.

The summit was attended by representatives of law clinics from the University of Jos, Nile University, Ahmadu Bello University, Veritas University, the University of Abuja, Prime University, Baze University and Philomath University, among others.

title: FG policies raise Nigeria’s exports by 25% – Dantsoho
excerpt: Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), says Federal Government policies and reforms have increased Nigeria’s exports by 25 per cent in th...
description: Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), says Federal Government policies and reforms have increased Nigeria’s exports by 25 per cent in th...
content:
Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), says Federal Government policies and reforms have increased Nigeria’s exports by 25 per cent in the last two years.

Dantsoho said this on Tuesday at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH) in London.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Mr Ikechukwu Onyemekara, NPA’s General Manager, Corporate Communication and Strategy, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen in Lagos.

Dantsoho said that Nigeria’s large population offered the country significant economic advantages, while recent reforms had contributed to increased cargo throughput and export volumes.

He said that the growth covered not only oil and gas but also manufactured goods, agricultural products, including cocoa and cashew, as well as raw materials.

He attributed the development to improved collaboration between the NPA and major terminal operators, including APM Terminals, which had enhanced operational efficiency, export volumes and port competitiveness.

The NPA boss said that the authority had established about four Export Processing Terminals to streamline export operations.

He explained that the terminals operated in collaboration with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargo was processed locally before shipment.

According to him, the arrangement ensures that Nigerian export products meet international standards and reduces challenges associated with quality compliance in destination markets.

Dantsoho said that Nigeria was better positioned to benefit from the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) through the reforms introduced by the administration of President Bola Tinubu.

He said that the reforms had strengthened the economy and attracted investors, creating opportunities for increased trade and cooperation among African countries.

He cited Nigeria’s growing trade relations with Morocco, particularly in the manufacturing sector, noting that the North African country had emerged as a hub for electric vehicle and smaller vehicle production.

Dantsoho also attributed Nigeria’s improved global port ranking to the reforms, noting that two Nigerian ports featured among the top 20 in the latest World Bank global ports ranking.

He described the achievement as a result of improved efficiency, technology adoption and effective collaboration with industry stakeholders.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The NPA managing director further disclosed that revenue generated from ports across the country had quadrupled, driven by increased cargo volumes and partnerships with international investors and terminal operators.

He said that Nigerian ports had recorded significant improvements in efficiency compared with other ports in West Africa.

Dantsoho, who is also President of the Association of Ports in West and Central Africa, acknowledged improvements in port operations in countries such as Tanzania and Kenya.

He, however, stressed the need for African countries to strengthen collaboration and sustain ongoing reforms to enhance the continent’s competitiveness.

He said that government was investing one billion dollars in the expansion and modernisation of Apapa Port in Lagos to accommodate future growth and improve competitiveness.

“Expansion and modernisation require collaboration with the private sector.

“NPA is working with APM Terminals and other major players with the required capital, alongside technology partners from Singapore and elsewhere,” he said.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Dantsoho also said the NPA developed a Single Window system in 2025 in partnership with a Singaporean firm.

He added that the authority was collaborating with a company in Abu Dhabi to develop a Port Community System aimed at strengthening business-to-business relationships and improving port operations. (NAN)

title: 2027: Ogun indigenes rally behind Adebutu, reaffirm ‘Ogun for Ogun’ agenda
excerpt: .pledge grassroots mobilisation as PDP candidate takes campaign to communities
description: .pledge grassroots mobilisation as PDP candidate takes campaign to communities
content:
.pledge grassroots mobilisation as PDP candidate takes campaign to communities

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Indigenes of Ogun State have reaffirmed their commitment to protecting the state’s political heritage, declaring support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ movement ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The residents made the pledge during separate engagements at the ward-to-ward campaign tours of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, across the state’s local government areas.

The campaign tour, which has taken Adebutu and Kolapo to various communities in recent weeks, is aimed at mobilising grassroots support for the PDP candidates and presenting their seven-point development agenda, tagged ITURA DE, to the electorate.

At the different ward meetings, residents, community leaders, market women, farmers and youths turned out to welcome the candidates, with several communities receiving them with colourful displays and enthusiastic celebrations.

The engagements also provided opportunities for residents to interact directly with the candidates, raise concerns about their communities and outline their expectations from the next administration.

Among the major issues raised were the poor condition of rural roads, unemployment, inadequate agricultural support and the need for improved infrastructure and access to modern farming equipment.

Several stakeholders pledged to mobilise support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ initiative, arguing that the state’s leadership should reflect the interests, heritage and aspirations of its indigenes.

At Alagada Ward in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a market leader, Mrs Folasade Ogunye, said her support for the movement was informed by the belief that indigenous leadership would better understand the challenges confronting grassroots communities.

She lamented the poor condition of roads leading to markets and the limited employment opportunities available to young people, insisting that residents needed a leader who understood their everyday struggles.

“We, the women of Obafemi/Owode, have suffered neglect. Our roads to the markets are bad, and our children need jobs. We want someone who grew up here, who knows our language and understands our struggles.

“We believe that someone with a genuine connection to the people will better appreciate our challenges. That is why we have pledged to go from house to house to mobilise support for this mandate. It is about our pride and the future of Ogun indigenes,” she said.

In a related development, some residents said to be former members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at Alapakooni community in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area publicly renounced their allegiance to the party.

The defectors reportedly set bunches of APC brooms ablaze to symbolise their departure from the party, citing dissatisfaction with its political leadership and questions surrounding the identity of its governorship candidate.

A community youth coordinator in Alapakooni Ward, Tunde Akinola, said their decision to align with Adebutu was motivated by their desire for leadership they could identify with and hold accountable.

“We decided to join this ward meeting today with our incoming governor, Adebutu, because we love our state and cannot trade its future on the altar of politics.

“We want to follow someone we know, someone who understands our people and has the capacity to deliver on his promises,” Akinola said.

Similarly, a community stakeholder and farmer at Onidunu Ward, Deji Bamidele, said farmers in the area were eager for a government that would prioritise agricultural development through mechanisation and improved access to farming inputs.

He lamented that many farmers still depended on rudimentary implements despite the increasing need to boost food production.

“In this community, farming is our life, but we have been left with cutlasses while farmers in other states are benefiting from tractors and modern equipment.

“When Adebutu explained the ITURA DE agenda and how agriculture would be mechanised, we saw hope. We are committing our farmers’ cooperative, which has more than 300 members, to the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ cause because we want our agricultural potential properly harnessed,” he said.

At Owode Ward 3, also in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a retired teacher, Alhaja Sariyu Bankole, described the movement as an opportunity to preserve the state’s political heritage.

According to her, Ogun State has produced several distinguished leaders whose legacies should inspire the emergence of leadership that understands the history and aspirations of its people.

“We cannot mortgage our heritage. Ogun State is the home of great leaders, and we must ensure that whoever governs us understands our history and respects the people.

“I have spoken to my former students and their parents in this ward about the need to participate actively in the election. We must make our voices count and work towards the future we desire,” she said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

In Sagamu Local Government Area, a youth leader, Comrade Bayo Oduwole, said young people were determined to play a more active role in determining the political future of the state.

Speaking at Ward 10, Oduwole maintained that the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ campaign should be driven by competence, accountability and a genuine understanding of the state’s needs.

“The courageous indigenes of this state have called on us not to surrender our future, and we agree with the need for leadership that understands our people and their aspirations.

“We know Adebutu’s family history here and are familiar with the contributions associated with his family. We also recognise the compassion shown by Iya Sunnah. We will mobilise our youths through voter education and door-to-door campaigns to secure victory,” he said.

Responding to the expressions of support, Adebutu described the ward-to-ward engagements as an opportunity to understand the needs of communities and build a development agenda around them.

He said the ITURA DE agenda was designed to address the socio-economic challenges facing the state, with particular attention to infrastructure, agriculture, employment generation and improved living standards.

“This tour has shown me that our people are yearning for homegrown leadership that understands their challenges and is prepared to address them.

“The ITURA DE agenda is not just a slogan; it is a social contract to restore dignity, fix our roads, empower our farmers, create jobs for our youths and return Ogun State to its rightful place.

“We are not just campaigning; we are listening to the people, understanding their concerns and taking note of their expectations. We will deliver on our promises,” Adebutu said.

Also speaking, the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, assured residents that a government led by the party would prioritise inclusive governance and ensure that grassroots communities were adequately represented in policy decisions.

She particularly highlighted the importance of women, children, education and primary healthcare in the proposed administration’s development plans.

“What we have witnessed in the wards we have visited is genuine concern and love for Ogun State. The people want a government that listens to them and responds to their needs.

“As a mother and a daughter of this soil, I assure you that our government will prioritise women, children, education and primary healthcare.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“We will not disappoint the people. This ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate is about building a state where every community, irrespective of its location or social standing, has a sense of belonging and benefits from good governance,” Kolapo said.

The PDP candidates maintained that their ongoing grassroots engagements would continue across the state as they seek to consolidate support and present their policy proposals ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

Peter Obi’s camp faces fresh internal friction ahead of 2027, with the OK Movement warning against division, and Datti Baba-Ahmed escalating his feud with Obidients.

As campaigns begin ahead of the 2027 general elections, the UK Coordinator of the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement, Adebayo Brown, accused leaders of the Nigeria Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council and the Obidient Movement of encouraging divisions among groups associated with Peter Obi’s 2027 ambition. The group said the NDC position is that support groups should support rather than assume party functions, and urged focus on grassroots mobilization instead of disputes.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Former Labour Party vice-presidential candidate Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed threatened to make further revelations about his former running mate Peter Obi amid growing tensions with Obi’s supporters. Speaking on Symfoni TV, he said Obidients are always eager to attack him whenever he speaks about Obi and claimed he has more damaging information about the 2023 election.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Peter Obi officially defected from Labour Party to the ADC coalition platform on Dec 31, 2025, after joining the opposition coalition in July 2025, according to analysis of the Labour Party’s future without Obi. Former LP chairman Julius Abure has now ruled out backing Obi in 2027, saying he would consider Tinubu or Atiku depending on a Supreme Court case.

title: Oyo 2027: Alli Unveils ‘My Pact’ Manifesto, Pledges ₦10bn Youth Fund, LG Autonomy
excerpt: The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Oyo State for the 2027 election, Senator Sharafadeen Alli, has promised to grant local government autonomy from his...
description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Oyo State for the 2027 election, Senator Sharafadeen Alli, has promised to grant local government autonomy from his...
content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Oyo State for the 2027 election, Senator Sharafadeen Alli, has promised to grant local government autonomy from his first day in office if elected governor.

Alli also pledged to make Oyo one of Nigeria’s top three state economies, establish a ₦10 billion youth fund and increase the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR) to ₦150 billion annually without imposing additional financial burdens on residents and businesses.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He made the promises on Tuesday while unveiling his manifesto, christened ‘My Pact’, to stakeholders in Ibadan, the state capital.

Explaining the document to representatives of community development associations, professional bodies, artisans, traders, politicians, labour leaders and other stakeholders, Alli said his pact with the people was built around seven pillars under the acronym Oyo AHEAD.

According to him, the pillars cover local government autonomy, advancement of infrastructure, health reform, education and employment, agriculture and export, digital economy and security.

He said the agenda was designed to transform the state’s economy and improve public service delivery, ensuring residents feel the impact of government across the state.

“Oyo State is the largest piece of land in southern Nigeria. We have 351 wards in 33 councils, and about eight million people.

“A state like ours should be feeding the South West and selling to the world. Last year, this State raised less than ₦100 billion as IGR. Ogun, our neighbour, raised nearly three times that figure.

“Nearly half of our people, about 3.8 million, live in poverty, by the measure of our own national statistics office. Our people work hard every day. With the right support, they can do far better,” he said.

On his economic targets, Alli said, “We will make Oyo one of the top three state economies in Nigeria. Our first target on the way is ₦150 billion a year of our own revenue, and the market woman will pay no more than she pays today.”

He added that his administration would ensure that every ward had a functional clinic, a good school and accessible roads.

“In every one of our 351 wards, there will be a clinic that works, a school that teaches, and a road that leads somewhere. The path there is simple. Power brings the factory. The factory brings the job. The job brings money into the home and the market, and that revenue builds the school and the clinic,” he said.

On infrastructure, the APC candidate promised to complete ongoing road projects and construct access roads to farmlands to ease the movement of people and agricultural produce. He added that every new road would carry a 20-year warranty.

He also promised to fully constitute the state electricity regulator to facilitate electricity generation within Oyo and provide dedicated power to industrial and agricultural corridors.

“On power, we will fully constitute the state electricity regulator, generate power here in Oyo, and send dedicated supply to our industrial and farm corridors.

“Faulty transformers will be audited and replaced every six months so that no street sits in darkness for a year,” he said.

Alli further pledged to restore potable water supply to 100 communities and connect at least 100 rural communities to electricity for the first time.

He said his administration would increase the number of state buses and modernise the Pacesetter Transport Company to improve public transportation.

On housing, he promised to work with the Federal Government and investors to provide affordable homes for working families, while reducing the time and cost of obtaining building approvals.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

In the health sector, Alli pledged to build a general hospital in each of the six local government areas yet to have one, recruit more doctors and other health workers, and consistently fill vacancies in hospitals and primary healthcare centres.

He said the plan would address the shortage of medical personnel in the state, noting that 10 hospitals currently had no medical doctor.

The governorship hopeful also promised free health insurance for infants, pregnant women and residents aged 70 and above.

He said he would target increasing health insurance enrolment from the current 271,000 to 500,000 within his first two years in office.

On education, Alli promised to reduce class sizes to 30 pupils, recruit more teachers, provide additional school facilities, establish skills centres across the state’s zones and enact an apprenticeship law.

For economic growth and job creation, he pledged to establish industrial parks, revive the Oluyole Free Trade Zone and create a guarantee fund to enable small businesses access loans.

He also promised to establish the Oyo Youth Fund with an initial ₦10 billion and build a digital hub in each of the state’s five geopolitical zones.

On agriculture, Alli said he would revive farm settlements, provide insurance for 10,000 farmers and work with the Oyo Export Council to establish a produce board to support farmers.

The Oyo AHEAD agenda also includes plans to restructure the state’s security architecture to protect lives and property.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Alli further promised to ensure that civil servants receive their salaries and entitlements as and when due, while providing them with work tools and improved working environments to enhance productivity.

content:
Ballot machines malfunctioned in a hotly contested House race in New York state Tuesday, prompting right-wing influencers to fling unfounded allegations of US midterms voter fraud even as local election officials insisted all ballots would be counted.

President Donald Trump and his allies have previously spread unproven claims about voting machines, alleging that they are faulty or unreliable.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The Westchester County Board of Elections said it was aware of an issue involving paper ballots that is preventing voting machines from accepting ballots at polling locations throughout the county.

content:
Ballistic Ventures, the cybersecurity-focused venture capital firm co-founded by former Kleiner Perkins partner Ted Schlein (pictured above, second from the right), is seeking to raise $490 million across two new funds, TechCrunch has learned through regulatory filings.

The San Francisco-based VC firm filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week to raise $360 million for its third flagship fund, matching the size of its previous fund raised in 2024, and another $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B. Neither fund had recorded any sales at the time of filing.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The fundraising plans come as the growing use of artificial intelligence has raised concerns about more sophisticated cyberattacks. The rise of AI agents has also created new opportunities for cybersecurity startups and the venture capital firms backing them.

Founded in late 2021, Ballistic Ventures’ founding team includes Schlein, former AT&T Cybersecurity president Barmak Meftah and Roger Thornton, who co-founded security companies Fortify Software and AlienVault. The firm has backed companies including Talon Cyber Security, acquired by Palo Alto Networks, and Pangea, bought by CrowdStrike, alongside startups such as Armadin, GetReal, Nudge Security and Oligo Security.

Ballistic’s ties to storied venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins, where Schlein spent more than two decades, help set it apart from rivals, a cybersecurity investor at another VC firm told TechCrunch. Its investment strategy, however, is similar to those of other cybersecurity-focused investors, including Forgepoint Capital and Ten Eleven Ventures, the person said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

In 2022, Ballistic announced its $300 million debut fund and raised another $360 million for its second flagship fund two years later. It also raised about $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund A, per PitchBook data. The new Fund B is targeting a similar amount.

U.S. cybersecurity startups raised $11.5 billion in 2025, the highest since 2022, a recent report by JPMorgan Chase said, citing PitchBook data. AI-enabled companies accounted for about 72% of U.S. cybersecurity venture deals through May this year, compared with 36% in 2019, the report said.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Separately, Microsoft, in its annual Digital Defense Report released last month, warned that hackers are increasingly using AI for activities ranging from phishing and social engineering to malware development. The technology is allowing attackers to operate faster and at greater scale, even as many of their underlying techniques remain unchanged.

Ballistic Ventures declined to comment on its fundraising plans.

The Department of State Services (DSS) has ordered an investigation into allegations by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar that the Service is organising protests in Sokoto State.

In a statement on Tuesday, the DSS said its operatives had been providing security protection to political actors across party lines, citing recent interventions involving ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Mannir Daniya, and New Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

According to the Service, its operatives deployed to protect Daniya evacuated him to safety when he was attacked in Sokoto on October 31, 2026.

It said two of its personnel were assaulted during the incident and were still receiving treatment in hospital.

The DSS added that Daniya personally contacted the State Director of the Sokoto Command to appreciate the operatives’ intervention and subsequently requested additional reinforcement from the Service.

The agency also cited its arrest and prosecution of Monday Udeme Steven in Rivers State on March 2, 2026, for threatening to attack Obi.

It said Steven was prosecuted before a Federal High Court in Rivers State and sentenced to two years in prison.

The Service argued that its interventions to protect political actors from different parties contradicted Atiku’s allegation, warning that such claims could demoralise operatives risking their lives in the line of duty.

title: Slavery was ‘monstrous injustice’ — King Charles
excerpt: King Charles III called the transatlantic slave trade “a monstrous injustice” Tuesday, opening a Commonwealth summit in which UK leader Andy Burnham is holding talks about apolo...
description: King Charles III called the transatlantic slave trade “a monstrous injustice” Tuesday, opening a Commonwealth summit in which UK leader Andy Burnham is holding talks about apolo...
content:
King Charles III called the transatlantic slave trade “a monstrous injustice” Tuesday, opening a Commonwealth summit in which UK leader Andy Burnham is holding talks about apologising for Britain’s role in slavery.

Britain’s head of state told the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda that slavery “still casts a shadow over these islands and other members” of the 56-nation group of mostly former British colonies.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow,” said the king, who is the ceremonial head of the Commonwealth.

“And yet history also teaches us that evil need not have the last word; that character and courage can combine to overcome the most monstrous injustice, as they did with the determination to end international trade in enslaved people, in which the Royal Navy played such a leading role.”

The comments come as Burnham uses his appearance at the summit to hold discussions with Commonwealth leaders about issuing a formal apology for Britain’s role in slavery, which saw about 10-15 million slaves brought from Africa to the Americas over four centuries.

Burnham, in office since July, said at the weekend that he was open to saying sorry but ruled out paying the financial reparations demanded by some Caribbean countries.

Britain’s pivotal part in slavery has long strained relations between the UK and its former colonies, including an awkward previous meeting of Commonwealth leaders in 2024.

The UK royal family benefited from the trade but Charles, who is also head of state in 14 Commonwealth countries, including several in the Caribbean, is politically neutral and is not expected to offer an apology.

A palace spokesperson also said “it would not be appropriate” for the king to announce a change in government policy.

Burnham discussed slavery with Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley during a meeting on Monday, one of several bilateral chats the prime minister is expected to have at the summit.

They discussed how Britain “was offering a structured dialogue for communities impacted by the transatlantic slave trade”, including the “next steps”, Downing Street said.

Burnham wrote in the Guardian on Saturday that he would have “difficult conversations” to safeguard the Commonwealth’s future.

“Listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state will form an important part of this process and I am open to them,” Burnham wrote.

He insisted, however, that reparations were “not the right answer”, saying British people today should not be “held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous”.

Instead, London is pursuing a “debt reset” plan for the poorest Commonwealth countries, led by former Labour prime minister Gordon Brown and which could alter interest rates on repayments.

Speaking Tuesday, Burnham told reporters: “I’ve been very clear that we do not support reparations… but it’s not the case that we don’t support countries in the Commonwealth around development helping them with debt issues that they’ve got”.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The UK will allocate £40 million ($54 million) over three years for infrastructure improvements in the Caribbean, including renewable energy.

The issue of slavery has loomed large over 77-year-old Charles’s ongoing nine-day visit to three Caribbean countries.

When the king arrived in the Bahamas last week, small groups of protesters waved placards reading: “Pay what you owe us.”

Britain has never formally apologised for slavery or agreed to pay reparations.

The BBC reported Tuesday that Britain was likely to apologise during its G20 presidency next year.

The country profited for centuries from colonialism and slavery, but argues it also led the way in the latter’s abolition.

In 1833, the UK parliament passed a law to abolish slavery in most of the British Empire.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Opposition Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has said Britain should not apologise, arguing it would boost countries’ claims for financial compensation.

At the previous Commonwealth meeting in Samoa in 2024, 56 nations signed a communique backing talks over reparatory justice after then-prime minister Keir Starmer tried to avoid the issue of slavery.

title: Reddit tests ads in search results as traffic declines and growth concerns mount
excerpt: Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing use...
description: Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing use...
content:
Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing users. On Tuesday, the company announced that it’s beginning to test ad placements in its search results pages, allowing advertisers to reach users as they search for products, recommendations, and other information on its platform.

“Ads in search may appear based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a user’s search query,” Reddit shared in its announcement about the new ad placements. “This is an initial test with a select group of eligible advertisers. During this test, we will evaluate and understand how users respond to these ads so we can refine the experience for users and advertisers over time.”

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The company offered examples of what sort of ads might appear, suggesting that a search for “espresso station” might display ads for espresso machines, coffee, or mugs, while a search for “home office setup” could surface ads for things like monitors, desks, and office chairs.

The ad test comes at a time when Reddit is reckoning with how AI has been changing the web’s landscape, and subsequently its reach.

Despite beating Wall Street’s estimates for revenue and earnings per share, the company’s stock dropped after it reported its third-quarter results last week, with fourth-quarter guidance that predicted sales of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below expectations of $1.05 billion. This was tied to Reddit’s declining search traffic referrals resulting from Google’s move to an AI-powered search experience. AI search now sends less traffic to publishers’ websites, as features like AI Mode provide answers directly on Google’s Search Result pages, reducing clicks to other websites.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Reddit also said that its global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in the quarter, and were down 2% year-over-year. The company noted that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low double-digit percentage by the fourth quarter.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

This leaves the company needing to earn more revenue from its existing users, which is where these new ads come in. The ads could prove to be more valuable to Reddit after it makes its planned shift to a logged-in experience, which was also announced during earnings. The company said it will make the transition gradually, initially in markets outside the U.S.

The decision to limit its content to logged-in users serves multiple purposes — it protects Reddit’s site from unauthorized AI scraping, and it increases its value to advertisers. Logged-in users are worth more to advertisers because they provide additional signals about their interests and behavior, allowing for better-targeted, more profitable ads.

title: Researchers warned of North Korean hacking tactics years before record $6.3B Binance heist
excerpt: Crypto giant Binance says North Korean hackers used fake social media profiles and the lure of a potential job offer as part of a months-long scheme aimed at tricking an employe...
description: Crypto giant Binance says North Korean hackers used fake social media profiles and the lure of a potential job offer as part of a months-long scheme aimed at tricking an employe...
content:
Crypto giant Binance says North Korean hackers used fake social media profiles and the lure of a potential job offer as part of a months-long scheme aimed at tricking an employee into downloading malicious software onto their laptop.

Researchers have repeatedly warned about long-running social engineering attacks that can go on for months.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

This latest attack allowed the hackers to patiently worm their way into Binance’s systems to steal a record $6.3 billion in crypto last week, the company has now confirmed. The hack, disclosed in an updated statement posted on X on Tuesday, prompted the world’s largest crypto exchange to suspend customer withdrawals across its network.

The FBI and blockchain investigators have blamed North Korea for the heist. The country has been long accused of carrying out massive cryptocurrency thefts in recent years to fund its internationally sanctioned nuclear weapons program.

In its latest statement, Binance said that North Korean hackers, posing as recruiters hiring for a job, contacted a software engineer who works on wallets at the company. Following two interviews with the purported company, the engineer was instructed to download an apparent coding assignment as part of the interview process. When opened, the assignment contained malicious code that compromised the engineer’s work-issued laptop. Binance said its security tools did not detect the malware.

That foothold in Binance’s network allowed the hackers to access an internal tool capable of taking over the work computers of two other engineers on the wallet team. One of those engineers had unwittingly downloaded a tampered app containing password-stealing malware months earlier after searching for the software in search engine results. While Binance replaced that compromised engineer’s laptop, the hackers used the engineer’s stolen credentials to break into the computer of a third engineer, whose job allowed them access to systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in crypto.

Binance said the attack “should not have happened,” and that it had improved its network security following the theft.

The hack underscores an ongoing tactic in the North Korean regime’s repertoire of attacks targeting the crypto industry and high-net worth individuals. Researchers have warned for years that North Korean hackers pose as venture capitalists, investors, and recruiters using dossiers of stolen American identities to trick employees into granting access to their systems.

These attacks are widely known across the crypto industry and have been the subject of repeated warnings from the U.S. government and cybersecurity giants in recent years. Some half of all intrusions at U.S. tech companies last year were attributed to North Koreans posing as remote IT workers and fake recruiters.

By Binance’s own account, the company faced at least 57 suspected attacks from North Korea, which it said reflect the “persistent threat posed by state-sponsored actors targeting the cryptocurrency industry.”

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

But how the hackers were able to convince the engineer into downloading malware given the highly publicized threat, and bypass security weaknesses in Binance’s own network, will likely be the focus of investigators’ attention.

While the case exposes how North Korean hackers use social engineering, such as offers of employment, to trick employees into granting access to their systems, it’s ultimately the responsibility of the company to ensure its systems cannot run unauthorized or untrusted software that could cause a compromise.

A Binance spokesperson referred to the company’s public statement but declined to answer TechCrunch’s questions on the record about the incident. Those questions included how Binance prevents unauthorized or malicious code from running on its employees’ laptops, if at all, and whether any third parties had performed cybersecurity audits of Binance’s network prior to the hack.

The company said it would bring in cybersecurity experts to review the incident and has put new security measures in place to prevent a repeat incident.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The heist remains the largest theft of crypto in history.

title: Orbital Matter 3D printed the first rigid beam in the vacuum of space
excerpt: A satellite built by the German startup Orbital Matter satellite 3D printed a half-meter long beam out of a custom plastic material, in what executives called a first for a free...
description: A satellite built by the German startup Orbital Matter satellite 3D printed a half-meter long beam out of a custom plastic material, in what executives called a first for a free...
content:
A satellite built by the German startup Orbital Matter satellite 3D printed a half-meter long beam out of a custom plastic material, in what executives called a first for a free-flying spacecraft in orbit, and a step toward constructing large structures in space.

The company’s small satellite, Replicator-2, was launched on a SpaceX rideshare mission this summer, with four of the company’s 3D printers onboard. Each printer can create a rigid, cylindrical beam by extruding coils of resin that are cured by an ultraviolet light, which the company analogizes to cement and water.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

This technology matters because future spacecraft will need to generate a lot more electrical power and radiate a lot more heat into the vacuum of space, particularly if they’re going to serve as orbital data centers. They’ll also still need to fit into the tight confines of the fairing on top of the rocket that carries them into orbit. If spacecraft are able to construct their equipment in orbit, the power and heat-dissipation challenges may get a lot easier to solve.

“Replicator 2 is the first proof that we can simply build the array in space, at whatever size the mission demands,” said Jakub Stojek, CEO and co-founder of Orbital Matter. The company is partnering with the European Space Agency and Thales Alenia, a leading European satellite builder, which it collborated with on Replicator 2.

Today’s large structures in space are origami projects—large solar arrays or telescope mirrors are folded up and then deployed on orbit. That’s a tricky engineering project, and so the idea of making and assembling those structures in space is appealing. NASA has funded some efforts at the idea, notably a mission with the company Redwire that 3D-printed structural beams in a vacuum chamber in 2023 but never got off the ground.

Two of Orbital Matter’s printers are designed to deploy a flexible solar array, but an anomaly led one of the printers to fail. Still, the boom that was created successfully deployed the solar array, and is an important proof of concept. Previous 3D-printing efforts in microgravity were limited to the pressurized environment onboard the International Space Station.

“That’s why we put so many printers on this single satellite. We preferred to learn in orbit and adapt the software as needed rather than waste years testing every possibility on the ground,” Orbital Matters CTO Robert Ihnatisin told TechCrunch.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The boom’s length is limited by the amount of resin carried onboard the satellite, and the company’s engineers believe that 100 meter booms are feasible. For comparison, SpaceX’s Starlink V2 satellites — among the most powerful mass-produced satellites in orbit — uses solar arrays that are 20 meters long.

Orbital Matter was co-founded in 2022 by Ihnatsin, who previously worked at 3D printing company FormLabs, and Stojek, and raised a $3 million seed round.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Now, Orbital Matter is working on another demonstration mission, scheduled for launch in 2028, that will test a larger version of its printer on a bigger satellite that the company hopes will deploy a solar array that can generate 5 kw of power. That will be a “stepping stone” toward  larger deployments of 100+ KW per wing by 2030.

The company is also collaborating with satellite builders that are considering incorporating its PADS (printer-assisted deployment system) into their spacecraft to extend solar panels, antennas, or other components.

title: Hiding inside Palantir’s skyrocketing quarter is a foreboding signal
excerpt: Palantir delivered such a huge third-quarter earnings report on Monday that its press release even bragged that the numbers were “crushing consensus expectations.”
description: Palantir delivered such a huge third-quarter earnings report on Monday that its press release even bragged that the numbers were “crushing consensus expectations.”
content:
Palantir delivered such a huge third-quarter earnings report on Monday that its press release even bragged that the numbers were “crushing consensus expectations.”

Yet, retail investors were lukewarm on the company on Tuesday, with the stock trading slightly down. That’s because Palantir’s enterprise sales, its big growth area, showed signs of slowing.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

First, the good news for the company’s investors. Revenue grew 96% year over year to $2.31 billion, the first time it has ever surpassed the $2 billion mark. Palantir’s revenue, which also grew 20% from the previous quarter, beat analysts’ expectations of $2.18 billion. Palantir also reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.44 versus analysts’ expectations of $0.41. The company even upped its revenue guidance for the full year. Normally, that alone would send a stock soaring.

The clincher was that Palantir’s U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever. The company reported $984 million in commercial contracts (up 148% from the year-ago quarter), versus $953 million in U.S. government revenue.

The reason for all this love from enterprises? They are signing up for the company’s AI software that can run frontier models and custom-train open-weight models securely, without sharing any of their data and business processes with outside AI labs. Plus, Palantir has always offered what is today known as “forward-deployed” software engineering, which helps customers customize its wares.

However, Palantir also revealed a less-than-rosy signal: Even as enterprises are moving faster than ever., they are often signing short-term trials.

“What Ryan and I are seeing on the front line and commercial is this much quicker interaction, much quicker to deployment, shorter duration of the contract but then an ability to expand that contract dramatically,” CEO Alex Karp (pictured above) told Wall Street analysts on the quarterly conference call.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Palantir is experiencing one of the unique phenomena of AI in the enterprise right now. Corporations are willing to quickly try AI software without their typical bureaucracy, but they are also more willing to cancel contracts.

Karp used one off-color metaphor after another to describe how unconcerned he was about holding onto his enterprise business.

“We’ve gone from being the most attractive person in the physics department to being the captain of the football team, kind of thing,” he said describing the influx of prospective corporate customers were flowing in. “Conversely, you know, once you go Palantir, you don’t go back, and that’s just that’s how it is, and you see it in our numbers.”



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The numbers don’t yet confirm Palantir’s long-term success. While the company closed a hefty $1.46 billion of total contract value from U.S. enterprises in the quarter, that’s actually a decline from its record-setting $2.13 billion of enterprise TCV in the previous quarter. That suggests decelerating sales, at least last quarter.

The next earnings will show if Palantir has solidified its role as a rising U.S. enterprise AI provider. Historically, many enterprises sign their biggest tech purchases in the final quarter of the year. Certainly Karp and team are confident. They increased guidance for U.S. commercial revenue to be “in excess of $3.559 billion, representing a growth rate of at least 143%.”

Mogging is about playfully upstaging someone or something

"Mogging", a word used playfully to mean outshining, outperforming or upstaging someone or something, has been named as word of the year by the Collins English Dictionary.

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

A fast-growing slang word among members of Generations Z and Alpha - both online and in everyday conversation - mogging went mainstream in 2026 with a 210% increase in its usage.

Collins' managing director Alex Beecroft said its lexicographers look at "how often words are used" and also "analyse patterns of usage" that reveal the latest linguistic trends.

The selection of mogging as word of the year, he said, "shows how each generation leaves its mark on language".

Mogging the Mona Lisa, whatever next?

He added: "It's a great example of how Gen Z and Gen Alpha have adopted a word and turned it into humorous slang, making the language their own and 'mogging' the rest of us!"

Mogging - not to be confused with mugging or mugging someone off - refers to outshining or dominating someone, most often in looks.

The word is often traced back to the acronym AMOG, standing for Alpha Male of the Group, and has been variously associated with bodybuilding forums in the mid-2010s as well as the manosphere and Incels.
