title: James Blunt on Traitors: I tried - and failed - to get banished
excerpt: He may have made it to the final episode of this year's Celebrity Traitors, but James Blunt says he did his best to get banished from the show.
description: He may have made it to the final episode of this year's Celebrity Traitors, but James Blunt says he did his best to get banished from the show.
content:
He may have made it to the final episode of this year's Celebrity Traitors, but James Blunt says he did his best to get banished from the show.

The singer-songwriter became a fan favourite for his 1980s leisurewear, outlandish conspiracy theories and military-style approach to tasks.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

A dominating presence at the round table, he characterises himself as the "yapping terrier" to actor Michael Sheen's "mature labrador", as they sniffed out the traitors.

Behind the scenes, however, he was playing a different game.

"We all get paid the same, whether you're there for day one or day 23," he tells the BBC.

"So for most of the time, I was trying to... get the hell out of dodge. But no-one was killing me and no-one was banishing me!"

Blunt's cavalier approach informed his gameplay. He knew that outspoken players are often snuffed out first, and that his best bet was to keep a low profile.

"But that's also really boring," he says. "And so for me, I just thought, 'Let's just go around and come up with theories.'

"You don't see it in the edit, but I was telling everyone, 'It doesn't matter [who goes], just kill them all!'

"It's fine, as long as you're apologetic when you get it wrong."

Blunt was partly responsible for James Acaster's banishment from the Traitors' castle

He was wrong more often than he was right. But in the penultimate episode, Blunt and Sheen stumbled on to a theory that the quiet contestants were more suspicious than their outspoken brethren.

In a pivotal round table, they turned their attention towards comedian James Acaster, and picked apart his story of a "murder in plain sight" that had occurred nights earlier.

Caught in the crosshairs, Acaster simply confessed.

"I was made a traitor without wanting to be," he revealed, as the others gasped.

Blunt says there was more to the sequence than viewers realised, hinting that Acaster was caught in a fib about a perfume bottle used in the murderous act.

"He didn't fall on his sword. That's what you saw, that's what you feel, but he didn't.

"You didn't see the full extent of the interrogation. It was heavy in there and it was clear-cut. He was pinned to a post. We got him. We really, really got him.

"I think how that played out hasn't really been revealed to you, but he didn't just say, 'Oh guys, you got me'."

In his exit interview, external, Acaster admitted the round table had been intense, but laughed off his uncloaking.

"It was sprung on me. It was a surprise," he said. "But I was glad that they caught me."

James Blunt and Michael Sheen were two of the most vocal faithfuls in this year's series

Blunt says the editing of the TV show is crucial to people's understanding of events.

And, with days and days of footage to sift through, not everything that happens  makes it to air.

"There are elements [of the show] where I was screaming at the screen for a different reason than you," he laughs. "No matter what really went on in that castle, you're a victim to the edit."

Still, some of his favourite moments made it into the show, including actress and model Jerry Hall calling him "smooth like butter dripping off of hot corn".

"That was a very special one," he laughs. "And she also said, to my face, 'I'll take you home in your wetsuit'".

And what about Blunt's confession that he greased his nipples with butter before every physical task?

"I'm amazed you don't do that yourself, Mark," he shoots back.

In the end, however, he was voted off the show in its dying moments, when comedian Romesh Ranganathan couldn't shake the idea that Blunt was in cahoots with the traitorous Maya Jama.

Blunt maintains he was blindsided by the accusation, but bears no grudges.

"The ending was perfect. It had all the twists and turns. I wouldn't have wanted it any other way."

The video for James Blunt's latest single, Circles, sees him riding through the streets and parks of London on a child's tractor

Still the question remains. If he wasn't that keen to go the distance in the castle, why did he enter in the first place? Was it simply for the experience, or did he simply want to promote his new music?

"I think you may have hit the nail on the head with the latter," he grins.

"I don't think otherwise I would have signed up to be imprisoned in a castle in Scotland."

There's a method in his madness, though.

In Blunt's own estimation, his eighth album, Airplane Mode, is his best work in years.

Now, musicians make that claim all the time. Blunt himself basically told me the same thing about his last album, 2023's Who We Used To Be.

But this time, he might have a point. After years of chasing radio hits and commercial success, he's gone back to writing from the heart.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The results are much more downbeat than you might expect from a man who's renowned for hilarious social media slapdowns and crowd surfing in inflatable dinghies.

Across the album's 12 tracks, he frequently sounds adrift, fretting about the state of the world and wrestling with "monsters in your head that you can't turn off".

"Darkness came like a tidal wave," he sings on the concerningly titled Reason To Die. "I'm paralysed by my body keeping score," he adds, over the portentous drums of Weight of it All.

The lyrics are informed by those negative, late-night thoughts that prey on your mind when you should be sleeping. Blunt says finally acknowledging them was a relief, after years of "trying to write happy upbeat radio singles".

"I don't have a therapist. I write songs as an exercise in voicing nostalgia and melancholy and the things I struggle with in the world.

"And, you know, the person you talk to the most in the world is the voice in your head. That's the truest conversation you're ever going to have, and that's who I was arguing with in the writing of this.

"I was going over the things that all of us struggle with: the burdens of growing up, growing older, having more responsibilities, having bills to pay, not knowing what the state of the world will be next year."

For all of his flippant humour, Blunt's demons are real.

In his 20s, he was an army captain stationed in Pristina during the brutal Kosovo war, and lost several close friends during the conflict.

Even after he left active service and became a successful musician, he was ostracised and ridiculed by his peers. He was later targeted in a tabloid newspaper sex sting, and was one of the many victims of the News of the World phone-hacking scandal.

The honesty of his new music reflects those experiences. And you can hear the rawness in his voice, too.

The musician who once quipped, "I sing like a girl, external", has a new depth to his vocals. On the new song Oh Daisy, there's even a Rod Stewart-esque rasp.

That, he says, is the result of a punishing 21-month tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of his debut album, Back To Bedlam (17.5 million copies sold and counting).

"I really damaged my vocal cords," he says. "I was pushing it too much, and my voice changed as a result.

"I actually now take singing lessons with different people – with an opera singer, even – and the [whole experience] has given my voice a bit of grit.

"Either that or my balls have dropped."

It's a typically self-deprecating jab. If anyone can laugh at themselves, it's James Blunt. And, however dark his new album gets, there's always a silver lining.

"This is not forever," he counsels himself on the closing track. "It's just for now."

"That song's a fist in the air saying, 'Yeah, we will endure'," says Blunt.

"I think I've been around long enough to know that I don't have to prove anything.

"The record label released my greatest hits album a couple of years ago, so if my greatest hits are already out, what am I doing now?



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

"I'm a guy on his own, writing songs with nothing to prove. That's a pretty good place to be."

Getting to know the real James Blunt... maybe

The jury has begun considering the verdicts in Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault trial.

The media personality, 51, has been on trial at Southwark Crown Court in London for three weeks, facing three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He has pleaded not guilty to all the charges. Giving evidence, he told the court he had been "obsessed" with sex in the past, but insisted it was always consensual.

The charges relate to allegations from six women spanning a decade between 1999 and 2009. Prosecutors said the complainants described him as someone who "didn't listen" when they said no, and "didn't care".

On Tuesday, judge Mr Justice Bennathan told the jury of eight men and four women he can only accept a verdict they all agree on.

Brand was one of the UK's most high-profile comedians, presenters and actors during the 2000s.

At the trial, he admitted using his fame to "facilitate sexual access", which he now said was wrong, but denied ever doing anything criminal.

His barrister told jurors that Brand "had an immense amount of sex", but that "none of it was unlawful".

He also said none of the women reported the alleged incidents to police at the time, and that allegations in a 2023 TV and newspaper investigation had "poisoned the well of justice" by prompting women to come forward afterwards.

Meanwhile, prosecutors depicted Brand as someone who saw women as a "disposable commodity" who "didn't matter to him" and were simply a "means to an end".

Barrister Riel Karmy-Jones KC, for the prosecution, told the jury that the women said his personality changed "from charming to frightening to nasty" during the alleged attacks.

She said the women, who do not know each other, had been "haunted for years" by their experiences.

One woman accuses Brand of raping her after they had met at the Labour Party conference in Bournemouth in 1999.

She claimed he turned from "camp, friendly and effeminate" to "monster-like" before the alleged assault.

When asked if there was any truth in the allegations that he raped her, he told the court: "No."

Another woman claims that the entertainer grabbed her breasts at a bar in London in 2004 before dragging her into a toilet, where he allegedly orally raped her.

Brand said he remembered going into the toilet with the woman but did not drag or force her there, or force her to perform oral sex.

A third woman had a consensual sexual encounter with Brand and another fan in his dressing room at the Hammersmith Apollo theatre in London in 2009.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

She accuses the star of later raping her after he invited her to his house in Hampstead.

She said she had agreed to vaginal sex but did not consent to anal sex. After he texted her six months later, she said she told him he had "treated me like an animal".

Brand told the court they had consensual sex, and denied committing anal rape.

The other allegations come from a woman who says she was pinned against a wall and groped; another who claims he put his head into her lap when she had been forced to give him a massage; and a complainant who says he tried to drag her into a toilet. Brand also denies these charges.

Brand's wife Laura gave evidence in his defence at the trial, describing him as "caring, kind and a wonderful father to our children".

Allegations of sexual misconduct against Brand were first made in a Channel 4 documentary and a Times and Sunday Times investigation in 2023.

He denied those allegations, which related to different women than those involved in the criminal trial.

Brand first rose to fame as a stand-up comedian and became a household name as host of TV shows such as Big Brother's Big Mouth, and with his own radio programmes on stations including BBC Radio 2 and 6 Music.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He went on to establish a Hollywood career, starring in films including Forgetting Sarah Marshall and Get Him To The Greek. He was married to pop star Katy Perry from 2010 to 2012.

In recent years Brand has reinvented himself as an online social, political and religious commentator.

title: Celebrity loses injunction bid but will stay anonymous pending appeal
excerpt: A celebrity who asked the High Court to permanently prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations of sexual misconduct has lost his case, with the ...
description: A celebrity who asked the High Court to permanently prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations of sexual misconduct has lost his case, with the ...
content:
A celebrity who asked the High Court to permanently prevent two news organisations from publishing his identity and allegations of sexual misconduct has lost his case, with the court saying the man's claim for an injunction was denied.

But the judge said a temporary injunction preventing the man from being named and the allegations published should remain in place, in order to allow the celebrity to appeal against the judgment, with anonymity and reporting restrictions remaining in force during the period allowed for any appeal.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

ITN and the Guardian have said they believe it is in the public interest to publish allegations that the man abused his status to engage, or attempt to engage, in "inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women".

The man, who denies the allegations, said any publication would be "highly likely" to lead him to kill himself, and that the court should prevent any publication or broadcast.

In his judgment on Tuesday, Mr Justice Nicklin rejected the injunction request.

He said: "The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make."

Nicklin noted that the man has repeatedly said he intends to take his own life if the allegations are published, and that this must be taken seriously.

He added these statements do not "establish that suicide is inevitable or that treatment cannot reduce the risk".

With a strict anonymity order remaining in place, it would be against the law to identify the man or publish details that might do so.

The man can now take his case to the Court of Appeal. Sara Mansoori KC, representing the celebrity, asked the court for time to decide whether he wanted to challenge the ruling.

She said that her client is "in a highly vulnerable position" and has "not been in a position to give us instructions on any appeal".

The claimant must lodge reasons to appeal by 16:30 GMT on 9 November.

The case raises highly unusual legal issues concerning whether a court should stop publication when an individual claims that a media investigation would lead to them inflicting harm on themselves.

The celebrity first asked the court in the summer to stop the publication of the investigation after journalists contacted him with allegations about this sexual activities with a large number of young women.

ITN and the Guardian said their investigation had uncovered how the celebrity had allegedly abused his "power and status".

During last week's application for a permanent injunction, Mansoori said making the allegations public would have a "potentially fatal impact".

The barrister told the court that the man had tried to kill himself after he had been contacted by the media organisations and was later detained in hospital for his own protection - but later absconded and tried a second time to end his life.

Those incidents of self-harm had not been because of the allegations themselves but the result of "long-term trauma and the fear of trial by media", she argued.

"The only reason [suicide attempts] would not be fatal is because the claimant would be locked up and prevented from his desire to end his life," she said.

Lawyers for the media groups argued that there was a strong public interest in allowing their investigation to be publicised because of the serious nature of the allegations.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

In his judgment, Nicklin wrote: "The proposed publications concern serious allegations about the conduct of a prominent person and the alleged  use of status, influence and access in dealings with women and girls.

"The subject matter includes alleged abuse of power, sexual misconduct and inappropriate conduct towards younger or vulnerable persons.

"Those are matters capable of making a significant contribution to public debate."

The celebrity argued that publishing the allegations would breach his protections under the European Convention on Human Rights, including articles that guarantee the right to life and protection from inhuman or degrading treatment.

However, the judge rejected the claim that publication would violate the man's right to life, writing: "No prior case establishes that the Court's knowledge of a suicide risk, together with its power to prohibit the event expected to increase that risk, is by itself enough to require the Court to act."

The judge accepted that publishing would cause the man "acute and potentially prolonged mental suffering" – but said "established law did not impose a positive obligation upon the Court to prevent that suffering by restraining publication".

The man also cited the right to private and family life.

While the judge acknowledged that publication "would interfere exceptionally seriously with the Claimant's private and family life", he also rejected that claim, saying a permanent injunction "would have been an exceptionally serious restriction upon freedom of expression".

The BBC Action Line website has information about organisations that can offer support for the issues raised in this story.

title: If hackers can take control of a supermarket freezer, how vulnerable is other tech?

description: Supermarkets across Europe have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers, and raising concern about the vulnerabilities of internet-connected ha...
content:
Supermarkets across Europe have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers, and raising concern about the vulnerabilities of internet-connected hardware from industrial machinery to humble domestic appliances.

Smart devices which are connected to the internet can include fridges, central heating, and even washing machines.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

And while that makes them easier to control remotely, in theory, any device which goes online can potentially be exploited by malicious actors.

However, that doesn't mean hackers can easily take control of it, and big brands generally go to great lengths to make sure their tech is secure.

Exploits have been found before in some devices. In 2015, researchers demonstrated how a vulnerability in a Samsung smart fridge could allow them to intercept internet traffic.

But there's no evidence domestic appliances are being targeted in the cyber-attacks which targeted supermarkets in November.

Ciaran Martin, former chief executive of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) says manufacturers needed to do more to make connected devices secure.

"There's a lot more that we need to demand of big tech to give us safer devices and products in the first place," he said.

He advised consumers to keep devices updated and enable multi-factor authentication wherever possible.

"I know it's a pain, but it only takes a few seconds," he said.

Since April 2024, UK law has required manufacturers of certain consumer smart devices to meet minimum cyber security standards, including requirements around passwords and security updates.

The NCSC said it was working with international partners and industry to understand the supermarket incidents, but it was unaware of any impact on the UK.

However, researchers from UK Cyber Defence have identified more than 800 refrigeration and building-control interfaces associated with British retailers that can be accessed over the public internet.

That doesn't necessarily mean they can be hacked, but it could leave them exposed to attackers exploiting weak passwords or software vulnerabilities.

The government has already held talks with senior food retailers about cyber resilience, following earlier attacks on supermarkets.

Helen Dickinson, chief executive of the British Retail Consortium, has said cyber incidents are a major concern for retailers, with businesses working alongside the NCSC to share intelligence and strengthen their defences.

It would not be the first time that hacks have raised concern about impact on food supply.

When UK supermarkets M&S and the Co-op were targeted by ransomware hackers in May 2025, the retailers struggled to stock some shop shelves with fresh deliveries.

Customers across the UK complained of empty shelves in the days following the attack.

Tom Hegel, a researcher at cyber-security firm SentinelOne, said retailers must be clearer about responsibility.

"The question retailers need to answer is who owns the security of that equipment, not just who repairs it," he said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He said internet connectivity can make everyday technology more convenient, but security needed to keep pace.

"Once an attacker can operate those controls, legitimate functions such as defrosting become tools for disruption," he said.

"Changing a setting can destroy physical stock, not just interrupt a computer system."

Outside of the home, connected tech is used to remotely manage industrial machinery and vehicles.

Cyber security expert Ken Munro pointed to a 2015 demonstration in which researchers remotely hacked a Jeep through its internet-connected entertainment system, prompting improvements in vehicle security.

"Fortunately, the vehicle industry woke up to this and fixed the problem," he said.

Mobile connections are also widely used to monitor equipment in power plants and water networks, allowing engineers to manage systems remotely.

Munro said UK utilities were generally good at securing these connections, but standards varied around the world.

His biggest concern was smaller, poorly funded utility companies which may still be relying on older, vulnerable equipment.

Without proper protections, "any factory or equipment" connected to the internet - ranging from carmakers to electricity or transport infrastructure - could face similar risks, said Olivier Daloy, a cybersecurity expert at Zscaler.

This is the latest hack to be linked to North Korea, which has been accused of relying on cyber-crime to help finance its sanctioned economy.

Blockchain analysts and the FBI have said the attack was led by state-backed hacking group TraderTraitor.

The FBI has called on industry partners to help block transactions involving cryptocurrency accounts linked to the group.

"The US has made a trite provocation of linking it with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea again," Kim Yo-jong, the director of North Korea's General Affairs Department, said in a statement.

Pyongyang has systematically built its cyber operations, recruiting promising students from universities and sending them to hacker units overseen by North Korea's intelligence agency, research groups like the S Rajaratnam School of International Studies think tank have said.

title: Apple unsure when it will get more foldable iPhones ahead of Christmas

description: Apple has said it does not know when it will get more of its new foldable iPhones back in stock as the company heads towards the key Christmas trading period.
content:
Apple has said it does not know when it will get more of its new foldable iPhones back in stock as the company heads towards the key Christmas trading period.

The iPhone Duo sold out just over a week after its launch, despite being Apple's most expensive smartphone at a cost of nearly $2,000.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The company warned of "constraints" in sourcing key components and admitted it was "really hard to predict when supply and demand will be in balance".

Meanwhile, Apple's new chief executive John Ternus said the firm was seeing an "unprecedented" price rise in memory costs, including chips, as the artificial intelligence (AI) industry continues to invest billions of dollars in building data centres.

Ternus launched the Duo after he took over from previous boss Tim Cook in September.

It is the smartphone's first major design change in almost 20 years but some buyers have reported problems with the Duo's screen.

Last week, the company said it would replace any handsets that were affected by an issue that caused a "small number" to crack along the inside fold.

As it released its latest financial figures on Monday, Apple's executives did not mention any problems with the iPhone Duo.

Ternus said he was "thrilled" by the early reaction to the foldable phone. Chief operating officer Sabih Khan said the company was working hard to get the Duo "into the hands of our customers as quickly as possible".

Apple's results for the three months to 26 September did not include sales of the Duo, which was released at the end of October.

Nevertheless, Apple said it had sold more iPhones globally over the last year than ever before.

iPhone revenue for the quarter rose 17% to $57bn (£42bn).

Sales of Mac computers also grew over the three months by 27% to a record $10.7bn.

Overall, Apple's sales between July and September rose from $102bn to $114bn. Pre-tax profit also increased, from $32.8bn to $36.1bn.

However, sales for both the iPad and Apple's wearable products, including its headphones and watch, fell by 10% and 7%, respectively.

Khan said that most Apple devices were still experiencing supply constraints driven in part by difficulty in getting enough microprocessors with advanced nodes.

Those components are essentially computer chip technology that allow Apple devices to operate more quickly, most of which it has manufactured through TSMC, which is based in Taiwan.

Khan said the problem was expected to continue into next year, particularly impacting iPads and Macs.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The situation has been made worse by what the company has repeatedly insisted is "unexpected demand" for its products.

Ternus noted, too, that Apple is still seeing "unprecedented" cost increases for memory, or the ability of devices to store data like apps, photos and text messages.

Much memory storage runs through data centres, which have experienced a boom in demand for space as AI chatbots and platforms - including those developed by the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic - have become popular.

Watch: Would you buy Apple's $2,000 foldable phone?

Storage prices have gone up for tech companies like Apple.

Earlier this year, Cook referred to a sudden increase in data centre costs as a "thousand year flood".

Apple has lifted prices on nearly all of its hardware products by around 20%.

Sunil Krishnan from Aviva Investors told the BBC's Today programme that Apple posted "a reasonably solid set of results" with a "pretty good performance" from its iPhone business.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

While there were concerns over the company's guidance on profit margins and the cost of memory chips, Krishnan added that in the broader context, "margins well north of 45% for a very well-established company, I think, are pretty impressive".

However, Apple's share price fell by 1.8% in after-hours trading.

title: UK meat industry hit by cyber-attack which targeted European supermarket freezers
excerpt: Sweden was among countries to report a cyber incident in which some supermarket fridge units had been hiked up in temperature
description: Sweden was among countries to report a cyber incident in which some supermarket fridge units had been hiked up in temperature
content:
Sweden was among countries to report a cyber incident in which some supermarket fridge units had been hiked up in temperature

Businesses in the UK's food supply chain have been impacted by the cyber-attack which hit supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe on Monday.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) says it is aware of "a couple of instances where vulnerable technology had been exploited in the UK."

The NCSC's chief executive Dr Richard Horne told the Today programme, on BBC Radio Four, that it had "worked through the night" to alert potentially affected organisations in the UK.

The British Association of Independent Meat Suppliers (AIMS) told the BBC some of its more than 300 members had unexpectedly become what it called "collateral" as part of the hacks.

Two members saw their fridges begin to defrost, AIMS said, while another saw their cold units rise up to 100C (212F) in temperature.

AIMS spokesman Tony Goodger said the affected devices were empty at the time so no produce was lost - but urged businesses to be vigilant.

The incident "must act as a reminder to all in the food industry at whatever point in the supply chain they are that their businesses may be seen by some as targets," he said.

On Monday, supermarkets in countries including Ireland, Sweden, Estonia, and Belgium reported fridges and freezers being hiked in temperature.

The events followed attacks targeting supermarkets and food suppliers across France in early October.

Hundreds of stores were targeted by the overnight hack, which spoiled fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.

Those attacks exploited vulnerabilities in some systems used to remotely control and manage cold refrigeration units that had been surfaced by cyber-security researchers months prior.

Horne told the BBC on Tuesday that it was still "too early to say" who was behind the hacks.

But he said it pointed to an urgent need for organisations and businesses to ensure the technology underpinning a whole range of applications we use and need daily was secure and up-to-date.

"That technology base we rely on as a society has not been invested on to the extent it needs to be," Horne said, noting many firms had extended systems beyond their end of life, not upgraded them nor kept them in secure compartments  disconnected from the internet.

Such actions can create vulnerabilities that many cyber-security experts say amounts to low-hanging fruit for hackers, and can be easily exploited.

But the UK's cyber chief said that they could be found and exploited more quickly and easily via "AI in the hands of our adversaries".

"We do need all organisations to look at what they rely on, to invest in renewal," he said.

"We intervene where we can. But, at the end of the day, it's your business. It's your charity. It's your life. You need to make the choice and choose wisely."

Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected in Monday's cyber incident, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.

Sabcobel, a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators, said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, causing them to warm up.

The same method was thought to have been used in last month's incident that hit hundreds of French supermarkets.

As with that incident, many of the retailers affected on Monday said they had no choice but to throw away spoiled food - some saying this amounted to hundreds of thousands of euro in lost produce.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Mathieu Tilman, who runs a Delhaize supermarket in Belgium, told the BBC he found it "truly distressing".

"There's so many people starving, people who don't have enough to eat. How can we end up throwing away so much food?"

"In moments like these, you just feel like quitting your job."

So far, there have been little to no signs of any such impact in the UK.

But the BBC has approached major UK supermarkets for comment and asked what action, if any, they are taking to safeguard against any similar hacks attempts.

"Retailers invest heavily in their cybersecurity and are currently working with the NCSC to ensure their fridges and freezers are secure as possible against potential attacks," said Graham Wynn, assistant director of regulatory affairs at the British Retail Consortium.

Asda, Lidl, M&S, Sainsbury's and Tesco are among the retail trade association's members.

Paul Chichester, director of operations at the NCSC, said at the launch of its annual report on Tuesday it was continuing to work with and monitor UK organisations affected.

"At the moment, the impact is minimal," he added.

"We're working with organisations identifying existing vulnerabilities in the UK and trying to get those closed before somebody exploits them."

content:
Hackers who stole a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from Binance used fake job interviews and a compromised internal AI tool, the firm has revealed.

Initial findings published by the company, which operates the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said hackers gained access to its systems through "sophisticated, multi-stage campaign".

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

It said they used a range of techniques such as malicious software downloads to compromise the computers of Binance engineers and gain control over tools to drain its wallet of billions of dollars worth of crypto.

Binance called it a "serious and highly sophisticated security incident" and apologised, saying "this should not have happened".

In a post on X, external, Binance said hackers targeted its engineers using social engineering techniques.

These see hackers use approaches such as phishing to trick people into parting with sensitive or personal details, that can then be used to try and access their accounts.

Binance said as part of the hack, one of its engineers was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform and invited to bogus job interviews with fake company representatives.

It said the perpetrators used "more advanced and deceptive" methods to build trust with him, such as sharing social media accounts that contained personal images.

The engineer in question was instructed to download malware masquerading as an "assignment" during a second interview, that deployed malicious code with "obfuscation techniques" evading detection.

Binance said hackers then leveraged the engineer's compromised computer and a compromised internal AI tool in October to gain control over two other engineers' laptops, and execute the next steps of the attack.

The incident led Binance to suspend withdrawals for customers globally, meaning users could not get their cryptocurrency out of the platform until the service was restored on Sunday.

Customers withdrew billions of dollars worth of assets after it reopened.

"We apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry," it said.

The company added it had taken a range of steps following the incident, including working with law enforcement to trace and freeze affected assets.

It said it had also set aside more than 100% of the funds needed to cover the loss, noting 98% of the token assets impacted had been "replenished" as of Saturday.

The record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) attack is thought to be the largest crypto hack to date.

US crime agencies, including the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Secret Service, have been assisting Binance in tracing the crypto taken from the platform's own wallets.

The agencies, along with a range of cyber analysts, said that the hack - like similar breaches before it - bore the signs of having been orchestrated by North Korea.

Kim Yo Jong, a top Democratic People's Republic of Korea official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on the accusations were another "sinister attempt" by the US to damage North Korea's public image.

The country has consistently denied being behind a number of major cyber attacks it has been blamed for in recent years.

The TraderTraitor unit, which is also known as the Lazarus Group, was blamed for a then-record $1.5bn hack of crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.

Binance had previously not responded to the BBC's queries about North Korea's alleged involvement in the hack.

But on Tuesday, the company wrote in its post on X, external: "The latest information released by the Federal Bureau of Investigation indicates that the Democratic People's Republic of Korea is responsible for this incident."

As part of its security efforts following the attack, Binance said it would also  increase investment in AI tools that can detect security threats, as well as engage third-party cyber experts to carry out a full-scale review of the incident.

It also said that it would seek to stablish a security research fund and work with leading AI and security firms on targeted initiatives.

content:
The Federal Capital Territory Police Command has rescued an abandoned newborn baby boy found wrapped in a nylon bag in Bwari Area Council, Abuja.

The baby was rescued on Monday, November 2, 2026, and taken to hospital for medical attention after being found in a critical condition, the police said.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The command’s Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a video shared on Facebook on Tuesday, appealing to residents to provide information that could help identify the baby’s mother.

Adeh said the newborn had bruises on his hand and one of his arms, adding that the police were making efforts to ensure he received proper medical care.

“We picked this baby in a very bad condition. This baby is a baby boy. The baby boy was abandoned, wrapped in a nylon bag, and he was badly injured,” she said.

The police spokesperson said the baby had been taken to hospital and would subsequently be handed over to social welfare officials.

She urged residents of Bwari to report any information about the baby’s mother to the nearest police station or contact the FCT Police Command’s Gender Officer on 08036259662.

Adeh also appealed to residents to provide information about any woman who had recently been pregnant but could no longer be seen with a newborn.

Addressing women dealing with unwanted pregnancies, she urged them to seek assistance from social welfare offices or the nearest police station rather than abandon their babies.

“If you don’t want the baby, you can walk into the social welfare office or any nearest police station and we will assist you. Instead of abandoning these children, come to us and we will help you,” she said.

The police spokesperson added that there were people willing to care for children and urged mothers facing difficult circumstances to seek help rather than expose newborns to danger.

Recall that in September, The Federal Capital Territory Police Command rescued two abandoned babies in separate incidents recorded in Kurudu and Gwagwalada areas of Abuja.

title: Nigerians talented to lead global sports — Shettima
excerpt: Vice President Kashim Shettima says Nigerians possess the talent and capacity to occupy leadership positions in global sports.
description: Vice President Kashim Shettima says Nigerians possess the talent and capacity to occupy leadership positions in global sports.
content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima says Nigerians possess the talent and capacity to occupy leadership positions in global sports.

Shettima said this on Tuesday when he received the newly appointed General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football, Samson Adamu, and the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, at the Presidential Villa, Abuja.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He described the appointment of Adamu as the first Nigerian General Secretary of CAF as additional proof of the country’s potential for international leadership.

Shettima said Nigeria’s sporting achievements had been driven by the quality of its people.

He commended the dedication of sports administrators and the institutions that discover, nurture and project Nigerian talent onto the global stage.

The Vice President congratulated Adamu on his appointment and urged him to distinguish himself through exemplary leadership and service to African football.

“Our nation has earned its place in the world of sports. We have flown our flag in arenas where few expected us to perform magic.

“We have made the impossible appear almost familiar, fundamentally because of the quality of our people,” he said.

Shettima, who conveyed President Bola Tinubu’s goodwill to Adamu, described him as a role model for young Nigerians.

The Vice President urged him to approach his new responsibilities with diligence, integrity and a strong sense of national pride.

He also urged him to promote, protect, project and preserve Nigeria’s interests, while wishing him success.

“Football especially is a uniting force in this country. Anytime Nigeria plays, it tends to subsume all other identities.

“Football and sports generally are a source of unity for our country. What binds us together supersedes whatever divides us,” he stated.

Shettima maintained that Nigeria’s diversity remained a source of strength, stressing that the country’s social and historical bonds were deeper than the divisions sometimes emphasised in public discourse.

He commended the often-unrecognised contributions of officials, coaches, talent scouts and administrators whose work provides the foundation for Nigeria’s sporting achievements.

“The minds that organise, the hands that prepare and the institutions that give talents a fighting chance are always not recognised.

“This is why from the bottom of my heart, on behalf of my Boss, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, we appreciate you,” he said.

He recalled the contributions of Nigerian football legends, including Rashidi Yekini, Austin Jay-Jay Okocha and Finidi George.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Shettima noted that their successes were made possible by individuals and institutions that identified and developed their talents.

Earlier, Dikko thanked the Federal Government for its support for sports development.

He said the administration’s commitment had helped enhance Nigeria’s international sporting profile and attract investment opportunities.

Dikko described Adamu’s appointment as a significant milestone for Nigerian sports administration.

He expressed appreciation for the Federal Government’s approval of Nigeria’s hosting of the CAF General Assembly and CAF Awards in November and December 2026.

According to him, the government’s support for sports had also strengthened the country’s ability to attract international investment through sporting activities and partnerships.

Responding, Adamu described his emergence as the first Nigerian to occupy the position in CAF’s 70-year history as a source of national pride.

Adamu pledged to draw on his experience as CAF’s former Director of Competitions to strengthen the continental football body’s administration and advance the development of African football.

He also expressed his commitment to supporting Nigeria’s efforts to harness its abundant football talent and realise its potential within the continental and global sporting landscape.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Adamu was appointed CAF General Secretary on Sunday, November 1, following a recruitment exercise by the continental football body.

He is expected to oversee CAF’s day-to-day administration.

title: Tinubu graduated with first-class in accounting — Education minister
excerpt: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a firs...
description: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a firs...
content:
The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a first-class degree in accounting from the American institution.

Alausa said he was familiar with the university, having lived in Chicago for almost 30 years, and had personally met several people who studied with Tinubu.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He stated this during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about the President’s educational qualifications.

“I’m telling you hardcore facts. I lived in Chicago for almost 30 years. I’ve been to that university so many times,” he said.

Asked whether he had met Tinubu’s classmates, the minister replied, “Oh, many, many, many, in person. Many. So forget the nonsense of…”

When asked whether the President graduated with a first-class degree from the institution, Alausa answered, “In accounting, of course.”

He also described Tinubu as a genius, dismissing questions about the President’s intellectual capacity.

“Oh, he’s a genius. Let’s not talk about the capability of this President. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is literally a genius,” he said.

The minister further defended Tinubu’s performance in office, claiming that the President had transformed Nigeria from a moribund country into a growing economy.

“Look at how he’s transformed a moribund country three years ago to a country that is growing,” Alausa said.

However, when the interviewer challenged the description by pointing to the country’s out-of-school children and poverty levels, the minister insisted that the conversation should remain focused on the President’s achievements.

“Let me focus on what you’re saying. I don’t want you to derail this conversation. But this President has delivered this for Nigeria,” he added.

Tinubu’s academic qualifications have continued to attract public scrutiny, particularly following the controversy surrounding his Chicago State University records during the 2023 presidential election petition.

The debate resurfaced in August 2026 after the Independent National Electoral Commission began displaying the personal particulars and academic credentials submitted by presidential candidates for the 2027 general elections.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Tinubu’s Form EC9, sighted by PUNCH, listed a Bachelor of Science degree in Business Administration from Chicago State University, awarded with honours on June 22, 1979.

The form also listed his National Youth Service Corps discharge documents, indicating that he served in Oyo State from December 1982 to November 1983.

However, the spaces provided for his primary and secondary school qualifications were entered as “0000”, with only his university qualification indicated in the educational history published by the commission.

The development renewed questions about the President’s educational background, with political figures and commentators expressing different views on the omissions.

The university had earlier confirmed that Tinubu attended the institution and graduated in 1979, with accounting as his major.

In September 2023, the university released Tinubu’s academic records following a legal request by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, who sought the documents as part of his challenge to the President’s election victory.

The university’s registrar, Caleb Westberg, also testified in a United States court that Tinubu attended and graduated from the institution.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

However, the university’s records confirm accounting as Tinubu’s major but do not specify that he graduated with a first-class classification. The claim that he obtained a first-class degree was made by Alausa during Tuesday’s interview.

In October 2023, a BBC fact-check found no evidence that Tinubu forged the Chicago State University diploma he submitted to INEC.

title: Otti urges teriary students to embrace leadership, integrity, discipline
excerpt: Abia State Governor Alex Otti, has charged students of tertiary institutions in the state to embrace good leadership, integrity, discipline and excellence as critical values nee...
description: Abia State Governor Alex Otti, has charged students of tertiary institutions in the state to embrace good leadership, integrity, discipline and excellence as critical values nee...
content:
Abia State Governor Alex Otti, has charged students of tertiary institutions in the state to embrace good leadership, integrity, discipline and excellence as critical values needed to build a prosperous New Abia.

Otti gave the charge on Tuesday during the opening ceremony of the 2026 Abia State Tertiary Education Sports Fiesta and the official unveiling of the New Abia Crusaders Club at the Umuahia Township Stadium.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The governor, who was represented by his Deputy, Engr. Ikechukwu Emetu, said the future of the state depends largely on the quality of character and contributions of its young people.

“The New Abia project is not limited to road construction, school renovation, healthcare improvement and infrastructure development, but is fundamentally about building people, restoring values, creating opportunities and raising a generation committed to excellence, integrity and service,” Otti said.

He described the fiesta as more than a gathering of students, noting that it provides an opportunity to celebrate youthful energy, intellectual excellence and creativity.

“This fiesta is more than a gathering of students. It provides an opportunity to celebrate youthful energy, intellectual excellence, creativity and the enormous potential of young people to contribute to the development of the state,” he stated.

Otti said his administration recognises education as one of the most important investments in the future of Abia and stressed the need for tertiary institutions to become centres of innovation, research and entrepreneurship.

He said his government is committed to producing graduates who are not just certificate holders but problem-solvers and job creators.

“We are committed to producing graduates who will not only possess academic certificates but also become problem-solvers, innovators, employers of labour and responsible citizens capable of competing favourably anywhere in the world,” he added.

The governor described the newly unveiled New Abia Crusaders Club as a platform for cultivating leadership, responsible citizenship and community service among students.

He urged the leadership of the club to organise mentorship programmes, innovation competitions and community development projects.

“I urge the leadership of the club to organise mentorship programmes, academic and innovation competitions, environmental initiatives and community development projects that will make meaningful contributions to society.

“Leadership begins with the choices you make and the positive influence you exert in your communities. Invest in yourselves, uphold your values and become active participants in building the society you desire,” Otti charged the students.

He assured that his administration would continue to place young people at the centre of its development agenda through policies aimed at expanding access to quality education, promoting digital skills and creating opportunities for productive employment.

In her remarks, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, Professor Uche Eme-Uche, described the New Abia Crusaders Club as an elite platform across federal, state and private institutions to promote responsible leadership.

“The New Abia Crusaders Club is an elite platform established across federal, state and private tertiary institutions to promote responsible leadership, integrity, service and positive citizenship among students,” Prof. Eme-Uche said.

She highlighted the achievements of the Otti administration in the tertiary education sector, including infrastructural development, improved staff welfare, clearance of inherited salary arrears and restoration of lost accreditations.

“The interventions have created a more conducive environment for teaching, learning, research and innovation. Members of the New Abia Crusaders must be properly informed, guided by good values and committed to making positive contributions to society,” she added.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Also speaking, the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development, Sir Nwaobilor Ananaba, said sports remains a vital tool for youth development.

“Sports remains an important platform for physical development, talent discovery, unity and the exploration of career opportunities for young people. The Sports Fiesta was designed to go beyond sporting competitions by providing students with opportunities to discover their talents and develop their potential,” Ananaba said.

On his part, the Founder and Pro-Chancellor of Lux Mundi University, Umuahia, Professor Gabriel Okenwa, who spoke on behalf of private universities, commended Otti for his transformational leadership.

“Good governance deserves commendation irrespective of political affiliation. Governor Otti has shown visionary and transformational leadership, particularly in infrastructure, education and human capital development,” Prof. Okenwa said.

In his opening address, the Chairman of the Central Organising Committee and Special Adviser to the Governor on Tertiary Education, Dr. Emeka Enyiazu, said the fiesta breaks institutional barriers.

“The fiesta has provided a common platform for federal, state and private tertiary institutions, including universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, to showcase their sporting talents. It is an opportunity to break institutional barriers, discover hidden talents and prepare young athletes for national and international competitions,” Enyiazu said.

He urged athletes to compete with courage and uphold fair play.

In her vote of thanks, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Tertiary Education, Mrs. Chinyere Okeziem-Nwoko, appreciated Otti for his commitment to educational advancement and youth empowerment.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Highlights of the ceremony included the official unveiling of the New Abia Crusaders Club, administration of oaths to athletes and officials, and a parade by representatives of various tertiary institutions.

The 2026 Abia State Tertiary Education Sports Fiesta was organised by the Ministries of Tertiary Education and Youth and Sports Development.

title: I’m getting back to my best, says Man City’s Foden
excerpt: Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden said he is getting back to his PFA and Premier League Player of the Season form ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League match at RB Leipzig.
description: Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden said he is getting back to his PFA and Premier League Player of the Season form ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League match at RB Leipzig.
content:
Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden said he is getting back to his PFA and Premier League Player of the Season form ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League match at RB Leipzig.

Foden won the Premier League and PFA Player of the Season awards in 2024 after scoring a career-best 27 goals in all competitions.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Speaking in Leipzig on Tuesday, Foden said he felt he was getting back to his best after a disappointing run of form which led to him missing selection for the 2026 World Cup.

Foden scored a hat-trick and laid on an assist as City beat AEK Athens in their most recent Champions League match in October.

“Consistency, just keep playing regularly, being happy, positive and being in the right positions to score as well,” Foden said of the ingredients needed to return to form.

“So hopefully I can get back to that level. I think I’m slightly starting to get back there now in my recent performances.

“So I hope they just keep going and keep getting back.”

“Being involved in goals gives you a lot of confidence, and when you’re playing regularly as well, you kind of just get into a rhythm and a groove.”

Foden said he had not spoken to England manager Thomas Tuchel since being left out of the World Cup squad.

“All I try and do really is focus on my own game, and hopefully one day the call-up might come back soon,” Foden said.

The 26-year-old local junior grew up a Manchester City fan but declined to comment on the impact of the Premier League’s charges against the club for breaching financial regulations.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Respectfully, I’d just like to talk about the game and not answer anything like that.”

Foden said he felt the transition from long-time City manager Pep Guardiola to new coach Enzo Maresca, who joined in the summer, was easier for him as he had worked under the Italian at youth level.

“I understand him more than the other players because I’ve worked with him in the past so that helps me try and help the team.”

Maresca agreed that Foden was improving and backed him to have an impact this season, although he acknowledged that the attacking midfielder was competing for a place with Rayan Cherki.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“I see Phil day by day better and better, for sure, 100 per cent. He’s going to give us many things this season.

“I said many times that Phil and Rayan are more or less in the same position, but again, I’m very, very happy with the way Phil is working every day.”

title: Army neutralises 2 kidnappers in Kogi follow-up operation
excerpt: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two suspected kidnappers and recovered two AK-47 rifles and thousands of rounds of ammunition during a follow-up operation in Kogi S...

content:
Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two suspected kidnappers and recovered two AK-47 rifles and thousands of rounds of ammunition during a follow-up operation in Kogi State.

The operation took place on Tuesday in Edimogbo Forest, Igalamela-Odolu Local Government Area, as troops continued efforts to track fleeing suspects following a raid on a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in the same forest on Monday.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lt. Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday in Lokoja.

Abdullahi said troops sustained their operations in the forest to locate fleeing suspects, clear remaining hideouts and restrict the movement of criminal elements.

He said the troops made contact with the suspects during the follow-up operation and engaged them, forcing them to retreat.

“The encounter resulted in the neutralisation of two kidnappers, while others fled into the surrounding forest,” he said.

A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines, 438 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammunition and 4,725 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Other items recovered included two bandoliers, two mobile phones and a power bank.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that troops had dismantled a suspected kidnappers’ camp in the forest during Monday’s operation, recovering about 1,000 rounds of ammunition and six motorcycles.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Abdullahi said Tuesday’s operation had consolidated the gains of the earlier raid, adding that troops remained committed to sustaining pressure on criminal groups.

He said the brigade would continue operations to protect lives and property and support efforts to restore lasting peace across Kogi State.

title: Tinubu fulfils pledge as Super Falcons receive $100,000 cash rewards
excerpt: The Federal Government has paid cash rewards to players, coaches and officials of the Super Falcons following their victory at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), c...
description: The Federal Government has paid cash rewards to players, coaches and officials of the Super Falcons following their victory at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), c...
content:
The Federal Government has paid cash rewards to players, coaches and officials of the Super Falcons following their victory at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), completing the reward package promised by President Bola Tinubu.

The National Sports Commission (NSC) disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Head of Press and Public Relations, Zira Zakka Nagga.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

According to the commission, each player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while each coach and official received the equivalent of $50,000.

The team had earlier received the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON) and three-bedroom apartments.

The Chairman of the NSC, Shehu Dikko, thanked Tinubu for fulfilling his pledge, saying the President had directed that all aspects of the reward package be delivered within a reasonable time.

“The Super Falcons made Nigeria proud, and Mr President has honoured his commitment to them in full. This means a great deal to the team and to Nigerian sports,” Dikko said.

He said the President’s action marked a departure from previous experiences in which some Nigerian athletes waited years to receive promised rewards.

“Some of our sports heroes endured years of waiting for promises to be fulfilled. President Tinubu has shown that things can be done differently,” he said.

Dikko added that the fulfilment of the pledge would encourage athletes to represent the country with confidence that their efforts would be recognised.

He also said the gesture would inspire young Nigerians, particularly girls aspiring to pursue careers in sports.

The NSC chairman recalled that Nigeria’s senior women’s basketball team, D’Tigress, received similar cash rewards in September 2026 after winning their fifth consecutive FIBA Women’s AfroBasket title in 2025.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Each D’Tigress player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while officials received $50,000 each. The team had also received three-bedroom apartments and national honours.

Dikko also cited the completion of rewards for the Super Eagles following their silver-medal finish at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations, held in Côte d’Ivoire in 2024.

He thanked the Ministers of Finance, Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, and Housing and Urban Development for their roles in completing the reward package.

“Delivering these rewards required close cooperation across government. We appreciate the Honourable Ministers and their teams for working with the Commission to complete the necessary processes,” he said.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The commission congratulated the Super Falcons’ players, coaches and officials on their achievement, urging Nigerian athletes preparing for future competitions to draw encouragement from the fulfilment of the President’s promises.

It quoted Tinubu as saying: “My promise to every Nigerian athlete is: make Nigeria proud, and come back to a grateful nation.”

title: Ogun govt, Ijebu Chiefs clash over Awujale Council as succession crisis deepens
excerpt: …State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing
description: …State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing
content:
…State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

A fresh controversy has erupted over the administration of Ijebuland following the decision of the Ogun State government to reconstitute the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC), barely a day after traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode announced the dissolution of the council and its replacement with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.

The development has exposed a disagreement between the state government and some traditional authorities over the appropriate legal and customary structure for administering Ijebuland pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale.

While the government insists that the AIAC remains the only legally recognised administrative body authorised to oversee the affairs of Ijebuland during the interregnum, the traditional chiefs maintain that the Adele Oba Awujale in Council is rooted in the customs and established traditional practices of the Ijebu people.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Hon. Ganiyu Hamzat, the state government said the withdrawal of some members of the AIAC did not invalidate the council or confer legal authority on another body to take over its responsibilities.

The government described the AIAC, established in August 2025, as the only legally recognised administrative structure empowered to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland until a new Awujale is appointed and crowned.

It specifically clarified that Chief Chris Okunowo and Alhaji Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, had publicly dissociated themselves from the reported mass withdrawal from the council.

Dismissing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, the government maintained that the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy laws of Ogun State.

According to Hamzat, neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the administration of the vacant Awujale stool.

The government also faulted the reliance on the Chiefs Law of 1957 by some former members to justify the emergence of the new body, arguing that the legislation was enacted before Nigeria’s independence and no longer applied to Ogun State, which had operated under its own laws since its creation in 1976.

To support its position, the state government cited a consent judgment delivered by the Ogun State High Court in suit number HCJ/180/2025, involving Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, against the Executive Council of Ogun State and 16 others.

It said the judgment affirmed the legality, validity and authority of the AIAC as the administrative body established by the government to oversee the affairs of Ijebu-Ode pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale.

The government noted that all members of the council were parties to the suit and had consented to the judgment.

It further stated that the court had affirmed that where there was a conflict between the administrative responsibilities of the AIAC and the traditional functions of the Olisa, the authority of the administrative body would take precedence.

The statement added that the judgment had not been appealed and remained binding on the parties.

Although acknowledging the right of individual members to withdraw from the council, the government warned that such a decision could not confer legal authority on another group to assume the functions of the AIAC.

It consequently cautioned members of the public against conducting official transactions or administrative dealings with individuals who had withdrawn from the council in their purported capacity as members of an alternative administrative body.

The government also urged the former members to refrain from actions capable of violating the law or threatening peace and stability in Ijebuland.

Consequently, it announced the reconstitution of the AIAC to ensure continuity in the administration of the ancient town.

The reconstituted council comprises Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, as Chairman; Chief Chris Okunowo, Bobasuwa, as Secretary; Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso; Chief Stephen O. Bakare, Babalaje; and Chief Alade Shote, Otun Balogun, as members.

The government said the council would continue to discharge its legally recognised administrative and traditional responsibilities until a new Awujale was appointed and crowned.

……..Chiefs insist on traditional authority

However, the government’s position came against the backdrop of a resolution adopted on Monday by traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode to dissolve the AIAC and replace it with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.

The resolution was reached at a meeting involving the Ilamuren, Pampa, the Odi and other traditional chiefs of Ijebu-Ode, where the leaders reportedly agreed that members of the existing AIAC should step down from their positions and assume membership of the newly constituted body.

The state government had established the AIAC in August 2025, about a month after the death of the 91-year-old Awujale, Oba Sikiru Adetona, in July 2025, to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland during the transition period.

The initial administrative arrangement was chaired by Chief Folorunso Kuku, the Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland and co-founder of EKO Hospital, Lagos, who is also designated as one of the Ilamuren.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

But in a resolution signed by the Chairman of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, Olo’rgun Dr Sonny Kuku, the traditional chiefs said their decision to replace the AIAC was informed by their interpretation of the existing traditional and statutory frameworks governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution.

They argued that the Ogun State Chiefs Law 2021 did not expressly establish an Awujale Regency Council or prescribe a general procedure for appointing a regent during an interregnum.

The chiefs, however, maintained that the Chiefs Law and the 1957 Declaration provided a framework for recognising customary arrangements, including the traditional institution of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.

The resolution stated: “Upon consideration of the applicable traditional and statutory framework, it was observed that the Ogun State Chiefs Law of 2021 does not expressly establish an Awujale Regency Council, nor does it prescribe a general procedure for the appointment of a Regent.”

It added: “It was further noted that the Chiefs Law and Declaration of 1957 provide an existing framework within which customary declarations are made and recognised, including the traditional institution of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.”

Explaining the decision to replace the AIAC, the chiefs said: “In view of the foregoing, a motion was moved and unanimously adopted that all members of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC) should formally step down from their existing positions and transition into the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.”

They further declared that the new body would assume responsibility for the administration of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum.

“Consequently, the Adele Oba Awujale in Council shall henceforth assume responsibility for the administration of the affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum and exercise, on an interim basis, such administrative powers and functions as may appropriately be required in the absence of the Awujale, subject to applicable laws and established customs and traditions,” the resolution stated.

The 14-member Adele Oba Awujale in Council comprises Dr Sonny Kuku, who holds the Ogbeni Oja title; Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Olisa; Chief O.B. Okuboyejo, Obasewa; Chief Chris Funmilola Okunowo, Bobasuwa; and Chief Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso.

Other members are Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osifeso, Olootu Olowa; Chief Jimi Lawal, Olotu Ifore; Chief Kunle Ogunade, Apebi; Chief Mrs B.O. Osibogun, Iyalode; Chief Adegoke Balogun, Jaginrin; Chief Agboola Alausa, Balogun; Chief Abimbola Okenla, Kakanfo; Chief Adebisi Adaran, Ogbeni Odi Awujale; and Chief Ayotunde Ola Odulaja, Lapoekun.

The traditional leaders described the arrangement as a recognised customary administrative structure designed to ensure continuity and stability in Ijebu-Ode while the process of selecting and installing a substantive Awujale continues.

“The Adele Oba Awujale in Council shall henceforth serve as the recognised traditional administrative body for the management of the affairs of Ijebu-Ode throughout the interregnum, in accordance with applicable laws, customary practices and the established traditions of Ijebuland,” the statement declared.

The chiefs also maintained that their decision was anchored on the customs and longstanding cultural practices of the Ijebu people, particularly those governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“Our position is firmly rooted in the ancient customs, established cultural practices and time-honoured traditions of the Ijebu people, particularly as they relate to the Awujale Chieftaincy Institution,” they stated.

They added that the resolution was intended to protect the integrity of the traditional institution and preserve the historical framework of Ijebuland until a new Awujale emerges.

.as tension grips Ibadan community

The Oyo State Police Command has arrested two suspects in connection with the killing of a 26-year-old man, identified as Kehinde Asimiyu, following a fatal altercation at Olodo Garage in the Lagelu Local Government Area of Ibadan, while reinforcing security in the area to prevent a breakdown of law and order.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The development came amid heightened tension in the Olodo community following the fatal stabbing of the young man, popularly known as KBlaq, by a commercial motorcyclist during a disagreement over transport fare, an incident that disrupted commercial activities and forced residents and commuters to trek considerable distances after motorcycle operators withdrew their services over fears of possible reprisal attacks.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, said the command received a report of the incident on 1 November 2026, indicating that the deceased had allegedly been stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde following an altercation between the two men at Olodo Garage.

According to the police, “the deceased was allegedly stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde at Olodo Garage following an altercation between both parties.”

The statement added that the incident subsequently came to the attention of the deceased’s family when “an unidentified motorcycle rider arrived at their residence and informed them of the attack.”

“Following receipt of the report, police operatives, accompanied by a patrol team, immediately mobilised to the scene, while the victim was rushed to Academy Hospital, Texaco, Iwo Road, Ibadan, where he was confirmed dead by the doctor on duty.“

“His remains were subsequently deposited at Adejare Embalming Centre for preservation, while photographs were taken as part of the preliminary investigative procedures.“

The police said investigations into the circumstances surrounding the killing had led to the arrest of two suspects, identified as Taiwo Babarinde, suspected to have inflicted the fatal injury on the deceased, and Ishola Semiu, suspected of involvement in the incident.

“Both suspects are currently in Police custody, while the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for comprehensive investigation,” the statement said.

However, the police intervention following the killing also witnessed a fresh security challenge, as unrest reportedly erupted at the Olodo Police Outpost, nearly resulting in a breakdown of law and order.

The situation was further compounded by subsequent reports of threats from hoodlums, prompting the immediate reinforcement of security across the area to prevent further disturbances and protect residents.

Consequently, the Commissioner of Police, CP Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, directed the deployment of additional operational assets, with personnel of the Nigerian Army, Amotekun Corps, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and other local law enforcement components joining the security operation.

The command said the coordinated deployment had helped restore normalcy, adding that there was now a sustained security presence in the area “to forestall further disturbances and protect residents.”

In a further move to address the underlying tensions, the Commissioner of Police directed the Area Commander, Moniya, to engage relevant community stakeholders towards addressing the situation and preventing a recurrence.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Acting on the directive, the Area Commander earlier on Tuesday held a strategic meeting with representatives of the Local Council Development Area (LCDA), leaders of tricycle and motorcycle operators, as well as youth leaders.

The engagement, according to the police, “focused on identifying practical solutions, strengthening communication with security agencies and promoting peaceful coexistence among residents and other stakeholders.”

Reassuring residents of the command’s commitment to their safety, the police said: “The Command reassures residents of Olodo and its environs that adequate security measures remain in place to safeguard lives and property.”

The command also issued a stern warning to those seeking to exploit the situation to foment trouble, incite violence or destabilise the area.

“It also issues a stern warning to individuals or groups seeking to foment trouble, incite violence or exploit the situation to destabilise the area that such conduct will not be tolerated,” the statement added.

It further declared that: “The Command will decisively deal with anyone whose actions threaten public peace or undermine the security gains recorded across Oyo State.”

The Commissioner of Police also appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid actions capable of escalating the crisis.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He urged them to “remain calm, shun violence and embrace dialogue as a means of resolving disagreements.”

He further encouraged community members to cooperate with security agencies by providing credible and timely information, while reiterating the command’s determination to sustain the prevailing peace and ensure the safety and security of all residents.
